body:
Fixes #977.

## The mechanism behind the whole issue

> **A job killed by `timeout-minutes` is reported by GitHub as `cancelled`, not `failure`.**

A run whose only non-success job is `cancelled` inherits the run conclusion `cancelled`, which on the runs list looks exactly like "a human pressed cancel" or "a newer push superseded this run". Grey, not red. No failure notification, no entry in the failed-runs filter.

That is why issue #977 describes the pipeline as `cancelled` rather than `failing`. The pipeline *was* broken — it just never said so.

**18 consecutive `CI/CD Pipeline` runs on `main`** concluded `cancelled` between 2026-08-03T18:09 and 2026-08-06T05:13. The visible damage: the newest GitHub Release was **v0.326.1**, while crates.io already served **0.333.0** and git carried tags for eleven versions in between. **Eleven versions were tagged and published with no GitHub Release at all**, and CI stayed grey through all of it.

## Root causes

### RC1 — `Auto Release` hit its 30-minute cap (run `31065367736`)

| Step | Window |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo build --release` | 02:53:54 → 03:02:08 |
| publish to crates.io (0.333.0) | → 03:04:52 |
| clean-install smoke test | 03:04:53 → 03:13:01 |
| free runner disk | → 03:14:16 |
| `docker buildx build --push` | 03:14:21 → **killed 03:22:04**, still at "Compiling fs2 v0.4.3" |

The PR-check `docker-build` job had used the GHA layer cache all along. The four **release** build-push steps had **no cache at all**, so every release recompiled the whole crate inside Docker — twice with Docker Hub enabled. `Create GitHub Release` sits after the Docker push and was never reached.

### RC2 — `E2E Tests (local web app)` hit its 15-minute cap (run `31073507682`)

`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` ran **10 min 36 s**. Every library Chromium needs was already *"the newest version"*; the entire time went to apt fetching **font** packages from `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` at ~30–60 KB/s. That left ~4 minutes for `Running 468 tests using 2 workers`; the job died at test 159/468.

**Compounding defect:** `globalTimeout` was `15 * 60_000` — *exactly* the job cap, which also pays for checkout, `bun install`, the bundle build, `npm ci` and the browser install. The job clock always won, so Playwright never aborted, never exited non-zero, `if: failure()` never fired, and **no report artifact was uploaded** — the one artifact that would have explained the run did not exist.

## Changes

**Errors**
- GHA layer cache (`cache-from`/`cache-to: type=gha`) on **all four** release build-push steps.
- `auto-release` / `manual-release`: `timeout-minutes` 30 → 60.
- `--with-deps` split into an `actions/cache`-backed browser install plus a **bounded, non-fatal** `install-deps` step — in **both** `test-e2e-local` and `test-e2e-pages`. Headless Chromium runs without those fonts, so a slow mirror can no longer end the job.
- `test-e2e-local`: `timeout-minutes` 15 → 40; `workers: 4` under CI (one per vCPU; these specs are I/O-bound).

**False negatives**
- `globalTimeout` 15 → 25 min, now well below the 40-minute job cap, so *Playwright* aborts first, exits non-zero, and leaves a report.
- New terminal **`pipeline-status`** job (`scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh`) that `needs:` **every** other job and runs `if: always()`. Any `failure` is fatal; any `cancelled` is fatal **on `main`** — where `cancel-in-progress` is disabled, so a cancellation can only be a timeout or a manual cancel — and a `::warning::` elsewhere, where a supersede is legitimate.

**Warnings**
- Every action off the deprecated Node 20 runtime: `upload-artifact@v4→v7`, `download-artifact@v4→v8`, `setup-node@v4→v6`, `setup-python@v5→v6`, `checkout@v4→v6`, across all workflows.
- `release.yml` was flagged as approaching its 2000-line ceiling. It is now **1948 lines — below its 1960-line starting point** despite gaining a job: six inline `run:` blocks became scripts, two of which (`configure-dockerhub-publishing.sh`, `invoke-create-github-release.sh`) were *byte-identical duplicates* across `auto-release` and `manual-release`.

## Reproducing test

`tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_977.rs` — **all ten assertions fail against the pre-fix tree and pass after** (verified by restoring the original `release.yml` and `playwright.local.config.js` and re-running). It covers: no `--with-deps` in any workflow, browser cache + bounded non-fatal apt step in both e2e jobs, `globalTimeout` < job cap, all four Docker steps cached, release budgets, the gate job's `needs:` covering every job (this caught a job I had missed), the deprecated-action sweep, and the shared-script extraction.

`gate_script_behaves_correctly_for_every_conclusion` runs the gate script for real across success/skipped, cancelled-on-main, cancelled-off-main and failure. `experiments/issue-977-pipeline-status.sh` is the same four cases as a standalone script.

Existing tests in `workflow_release.rs` and `issue_717.rs` were updated to follow the extracted logic into the scripts rather than dropped.

## Evidence and analysis

`dev/log/issues/977/pulls/978/` — both full run logs (25 609 and 31 816 lines) with per-step timings, run/annotation dumps, and **`ANALYSIS.md`** with the timeline, per-requirement root cause, prior art considered (`re-actors/alls-green`, `technote-space/workflow-conclusion-action`) and why a 20-line script fits better.

## Upstream reports

The same defects exist in the pipeline templates, so they are filed there with reproducible examples, workarounds and code fixes:

- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#118, link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#123, link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#50 — timeout-reported-as-cancelled (all three templates; verified none has an aggregate gate).
- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#119 — uncached release Docker builds. **Verified as rust-only**: the js and python templates have a single, already-cached build step, so this was not reported against them.

Template job-set diff: the rust template has `cargo-lock`, `coverage`, `deploy-docs` and `fresh-merge` as separate jobs. formal-ai already covers all four — fresh-merge via `scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh`, Cargo.lock verification in `lint`, and coverage in its own `coverage.yml` (split out under #895 for the same line-limit reason).

## Local verification

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `shellcheck --severity=warning` over all 18 tracked scripts, `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs`, and `cargo test --test unit ci_cd` (**172 passed, 0 failed**) all clean.

## Not addressed, deliberately

- **Recovering the 11 missing GitHub Releases** (v0.326.2 … v0.333.0). The tags and crates.io versions exist; backfilling the Releases is a one-off `gh release create` sweep over historical tags, not a pipeline change, and it rewrites public release history — worth doing, but as its own decision rather than folded into this PR.
- **~25 source files in the 900–1000-line warning band** (`src/main.rs`, `src/solver.rs`, `tests/source/calculation.rs`, …). These are long-standing, predate this issue, and are only warnings; splitting them would be a large, risky refactor unrelated to the CI/CD failures. `scripts/check-file-size.rs` only reports warnings for files that *grew*, so they do not fire on unrelated PRs.
title: fix(ci): stop CI/CD timeouts from hiding as cancelled runs

body:
## Summary

- identify the repeated Intel macOS failure as a 35-minute capacity boundary, then split that lane into complementary `core` and `specification` shards without raising its timeout or dropping coverage
- move concurrency from mixed workflows to individual jobs, retaining cancellation for superseded reads while placing every material repository writer in a non-lossy `queue: max` scope
- eliminate current warning debt: use the supported Pages timeout, classify intentional exemptions/reports as notices, and bring all five flagged files below their warning thresholds
- add the missing CodeQL, dependency-review, and live-link gates; repair five stale documentation links and keep Wayback diagnostic-only so archived copies cannot make dead live links pass
- enable the repository's Dependency Graph prerequisite after the first remote Dependency Review run exposed that settings-level gap; SBOM export and base/head comparison now succeed
- preserve the complete issue/PR/run/template investigation, root-cause analysis, timeline, alternatives, source research, and verification logs in a SHA-256-manifested evidence archive
- strengthen the split-seed regression after the first full remote lint run correctly required language-matrix coverage; all four moved intents are now checked for every registered locale and every runtime loader
- fix a fresh link-gate finding: replace a repeatedly unavailable reference with live university course material, and prevent the Wayback helper from misreporting Lychee's successful redirects as broken links

## Root causes

The latest default-branch pipeline had no failed or hanging test. Its Intel macOS job was still producing passing specification results when GitHub killed it at the unchanged 35-minute limit. The last successful instance already took 28m37s, so cold build time plus the growing monolithic suite had exhausted the remaining margin.

The wider audit also found a cancellation-scope defect: read checks and write jobs shared workflow-level concurrency. A newer run could interrupt an active writer, and GitHub's default one-pending-run behavior could replace an older queued writer. Job-level concurrency now matches side-effect boundaries.

A fresh link run found one real 502 and 18 healthy redirects. The copied template helper parsed every Markdown bullet across both sections and announced 19 broken URLs. It now parses only Lychee's error section (with a compatibility fallback), covered by a red/green Node regression; the unavailable source was replaced rather than ignored or excused by its archive.

The complete root-cause analysis and all nine issue requirements are mapped in the [durable evidence report](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-999-31976d2c6ce9/dev/log/issues/999/pulls/1000/README.md).

## Verification

- issue #999 regressions: 6/6
- complete CI/CD unit module: 183/183
- all-features repository tests: 2,664 passed, 3 intentionally ignored, 0 failed in the final 2,667-test target; all integration executables and doc tests passed
- self-AST census: 8/8; browser suite: 53/53
- Clippy with warnings denied, examples, normal/docs.rs rustdoc, formatting, actionlint 1.7.12, ShellCheck, changelog reconstruction, fragment mapping, file-size enforcement, diff check, and repository secret scan: passed
- local link gates: 1,071 checked before the remote probe changed; clean-tree rerun after replacement: 991 current inputs, 0 errors
- diff-aware language-test-coverage gate: `en`, `ru`, `hi`, `zh`, and `es` covered
- evidence manifest: all archived files verified
- final GitHub Actions: 11/11 workflows succeeded on head `04e81c274a22b66a9093f20072ccf5dc43118ec0` (58 checks, 0 non-passing)

The minimum regression ran before implementation and failed on the missing sharding, writer queues, gates, and size bounds; it passes after the fix. Full logs are in the evidence report and the [readable case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-999-31976d2c6ce9/docs/case-studies/issue-999/README.md).

No visual UI behavior changed, so screenshots do not apply.

## Upstream reports

- corrected the Rust template's obsolete concurrency conclusion in [issue 113](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/113#issuecomment-5257178147)
- reported the shared archived-link false negative with reproductions, workarounds, and code fixes in [Rust #125](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/125), [JavaScript #127](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/127), and [Python #54](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/54)
- reported the shared redirect-parser false positive in [Rust #126](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/126) and [JavaScript #128](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/128)

Fixes #999

## Summary

- preserve the upstream signature of the bundled Playwright browser during macOS Electron signing, fixing both x64 and arm64 package failures
- enforce warning-free Rust builds across Cargo and direct `rustc` release paths, while correctly scoping intentional WASM dead code and Unix-only state
- bundle the VS Code extension's runtime JavaScript and exclude `node_modules`, reducing the VSIX from 9,015 files to 481 files and removing the oversized-file-count warning
- validate the locked dependency graph and smoke-test the exact published crate in both automatic and manual release paths
- keep forensic `dev/log` snapshots outside source-size policy and prevent parallel E2E jobs from racing to save the same Bun executable cache
- capture the complete issue, PR, CI, template-comparison, timeline, root-cause, and external-research evidence under `dev/log/issues/798/pulls/799`

## Reproduction and root causes

The preserved failing runs showed three independent defects:

1. `@electron/osx-sign` recursively signed Chrome for Testing's already-signed framework children, producing `unsealed contents present in the root directory` on both macOS architectures.
2. `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings` did not reach the direct `rustc` WASM invocation, and shared-memory state was declared on Windows despite only being consumed by Unix cleanup.
3. VSIX packaging copied the complete dependency tree, yielding 9,015 files, 4,608 JavaScript files, and a 192.81 MB archive.

The earlier Auto Release self-hosting failure was a valid provenance ratchet failure rather than a false positive. Every implementation commit in this PR includes a `Formal-AI-Session` trailer and points to the committed evidence ledger; the local metric now reports 90.60%.

Detailed chronology and requirement mapping: `dev/log/issues/798/pulls/799/timeline-root-causes.md`.

## Verification

- `cargo test --all-features` — 1,852 passed, 2 ignored
- `cargo test --test unit ci_cd::issue_798` — 8 passed
- `rust-script --test scripts/check-file-size.rs` — 12 passed
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- macOS signing regression tests — 2 passed
- VS Code extension tests — 51 passed
- Node 22 clean install, resource preparation, standalone bundle load, smoke test, and VSIX packaging
- direct WASM `rustc` build with warnings denied
- `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1`
- self-hosting metric since `v0.299.0` — 90.60%

The authored code diff is whitespace-clean. Verbatim CI logs intentionally retain their original whitespace as forensic evidence.

body:
Follow-up to #909 (closed by #966).

## Status after the merge with `main`

`main`'s PR #966 (epic E69 / issue #916) landed the two **write-side** halves of #909 while this PR was open:

- gemini's `~/.gemini/settings.json` companion file (`security.auth.selectedType`), via `companion "<path>"` seed nodes → `ClientIntegrationCompanionFile` → `write_companion_file`;
- qwen's `shell_env "OPENAI_MODEL={model}"`.

This branch had implemented the same two fixes with a *different* data model (a recursive `companions: Vec<Self>`), which is what produced the merge conflict. The conflict is resolved by **adopting `main`'s canonical mechanism** and dropping the duplicate; what remains unique to this PR is the third suggestion in the issue, which `main` does not have: **verifying after configuring**.

## Problem this PR still closes

`--global` reported success and exited 0 without ever re-reading what it wrote, so it could only report what it *intended* to write, never what a client would find. A future drift of the same kind — an export renamed upstream, a settings key moved — silently produces a "configured" client that fails later with an unrelated startup error.

## Fix — the contract as data, checked by reading back

- `headless_require "<kind>=<target>"` declares the startup contract **apart** from the settings that write it, on both `ClientIntegrationGlobalConfig` and `ClientIntegrationCompanionFile` (`env` names an exported variable; `json`/`toml` name `<relative path>:<dotted key>`);
- `auth_refusal "<text>"` entries in each client's `verification` block name the outputs that mean "not configured".

`src/client_integrations/global_verify.rs` consumes that data at two levels:

- **always on** — after every `--global` run, `verify_written_config` re-reads each declared requirement from disk (the tool's own managed block in the shell profile, or a dotted JSON/TOML key) and fails the run when one is missing or empty. No client needed, so it is safe offline and in CI.
- **opt in** — `formal-ai with --global --verify <tool>` runs `probe_headless_start`: it starts the configured client once non-interactively, sourcing the shell profile, and fails when the output matches a seeded auth refusal. A client that is not installed is skipped, not failed.

All user-facing text lives in `data/seed/multilingual-responses-client-config.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh/es) per the R379 doctrine.

## Reproduction

```sh
./experiments/issue-909-headless-config-gaps.sh   # configures into a throwaway HOME, exits 1 on any missing requirement
```

## Tests

- `tests/integration/with_formal_ai_headless_global.rs` — 7 tests: the gemini settings file is written / preserved / restored on `--undo`, qwen gets the complete triple inside its own managed block (an operator-owned export outside the block does not count), `--verify` fails on a refusing client and passes on a starting one, `--verify` is rejected without `--global`, and a whole-task sweep runs `--global --all --verify` and asserts **every** registry-declared requirement of **every** client is materialised.
- `tests/unit/docs_requirements_issue_909.rs` — R909-1..R909-6 traceability plus the four `client_global_config_*` intents answering in every registered language.
- Red/green evidence and the raw issue data are preserved in `docs/case-studies/issue-909/`.

## Docs

`REQUIREMENTS.md` (R909-1..R909-6, with R909-1/R909-2 attributed to the code that landed on `main` for R916-08a/R916-08b), `docs/requirements-traceability.md`, `README.md`, and a `changelog.d/` fragment (`bump: minor`).


## Review follow-up — `data/seed` conflicts in almost every PR

> we also need to find a way to automatically (using script, that should be saved
> somewhere) reorganize ./data/seed in such a way that, probability of conflicts is
> drastically reduced

The cause is not volume, it is *sequential* sharding. `scripts/close-total.py` filled
`data/seed/closure-generated-NN.lino` in sorted order up to a 1400-line cap, so each
shard's contents depended on the total **size** of every block sorted before it. One
new token rewrote the tail of its own shard and pushed a block into each following
shard. Measured on the pre-fix tree (`198b11cd`, 11 shards), adding a single token:

| new token | shards dirtied |
|---|---|
| `aaa_shard_probe` | **11 / 11** |
| `mmm_shard_probe` | 9 / 11 |
| `sss_shard_probe` | 2 / 11 |
| `zzz_shard_probe` | 1 / 11 |

Two branches each defining one mid-alphabet token therefore overlapped almost
everywhere — hence a conflict in nearly every pull request.

### Fix — content-addressed shards

Each meaning is now placed by a digest of its own slug, `sha256(slug) % SHARD_COUNT`,
over a **fixed** shard count (16) rather than one derived from the corpus size. A
block's file is a function of the block alone, so adding, removing or reparenting a
token touches exactly one shard and leaves the other 15 byte-identical:

| new token | shards dirtied (after) |
|---|---|
| `aaa_shard_probe` | 1 / 16 |
| `mmm_shard_probe` | 1 / 16 |
| `sss_shard_probe` | 1 / 16 |
| `zzz_shard_probe` | 1 / 16 |

Shards land at ~810–990 lines with headroom to the 1500-line data-file limit;
`close-total.py` now **fails** rather than silently overflowing if one exceeds the
budget, telling you to raise `SHARD_COUNT`. Every shard is written even when empty so
the file set stays stable too.

- `experiments/issue-909-seed-shard-conflict-blast-radius.sh` — reproduces the table
  above: asserts the committed shards are idempotent, then adds one token at four
  points in the sort order and fails if any dirties more than one file (or zero, which
  would mean the probe proved nothing).
- `tests/unit/total_closure.rs::generated_closure_shards_are_content_addressed` — CI
  gate pinning every committed meaning to the shard its digest selects, so a future
  refactor cannot quietly restore size-dependent packing. The symptom shows up in
  *other* people's branches, so it would otherwise go unnoticed.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents the invariant and when to raise `SHARD_COUNT`.

## Merge with `main`

Resolved: the conflicts were confined to generated artifacts
(`closure-generated-*.lino`, `data/meta/self-ast/`), so they were resolved by
regeneration — `python3 scripts/close-total.py` (`unresolved_distinct: 0`) and
`cargo run --example regenerate_self_ast_census`.

Fixes #909

body:
## Summary

Fixes the CI/CD defects behind issue #808 and moves the checks that previously
only ran on `main` into the pull-request stage, so a pull request can no longer
be green while the release it produces is broken.

Fixes #808

## Root causes found (evidence in `dev/log/issues/808/pulls/809/`)

1. **macOS codesign failure on release** — `codesign` refused the bundled Chrome
   for Testing runtime ("unsealed contents present in the root directory of an
   embedded framework"): its framework layout is not versioned. Fixed with
   `mac.signIgnore`, independently of the custom sign hook.
2. **The macOS sign hook produced no output at all** — this was unexplained, so
   the first commit added an unconditional hook-entry banner and routed the
   diagnostics to stderr. On the first pull-request packaging run that
   instrumentation answered it: `app-builder-lib`'s `isSignAllowed()` returns
   early with *"Current build is a part of pull request, code signing will be
   skipped"* whenever `GITHUB_BASE_REF` is set, so the hook is never invoked and
   the app ships without a `CodeResources` envelope. Fixed with
   `CSC_FOR_PULL_REQUEST` on the ad-hoc step only (no secrets are in play there).
3. **Auto Release blocked by a malformed self-hosting evidence trailer** — now
   validated at pull-request time by a new `evidence-check` job.

## All checks now run at the pull-request stage (issue comment 5020083365)

- Desktop + `.vsix` packaging: the full six-target matrix, macOS signing and the
  artifact smoke tests run on pull requests in **dry-run** mode — every
  publishing step (attest, release upload, `SHA256SUMS`, `finalize`) is skipped.
  Path-filtered so unrelated pull requests do not pay for six runners.
- Docker image build + `verify-formal-ai-dind` runtime contract (`push: false`,
  so it is fork-safe).
- Self-hosting evidence trailers.
- Secrets scan.
- Fresh-merge simulation against the current `main`.

## Practices adopted from the pipeline templates (R3/R5)

Compared against `link-foundation/{rust,js,python}-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`
and `hive-mind/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`:

- `scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` (verbatim from the js template) — a stale
  merge preview now fails the pull request instead of breaking `main`.
- `scripts/check-secrets.sh` + `.secretlintrc.json`. Scoped to the files a change
  touches: the template's `secretlint "**/*"` did not finish in 25 minutes on
  this tree, while the diff scan measures 2.6 s. Verified it actually fires — a
  planted `ghp_…` token is reported as `[GITHUB_TOKEN] found GitHub Token`.
- `.github/actions/setup-buildx-resilient` (verbatim from the rust template),
  replacing all three raw `docker/setup-buildx-action@v4` uses.
- Replaced all nine `always() && !cancelled()` guards with `!cancelled()`
  (best-practices §10): `always()` also runs the job when the run is *cancelled*,
  which is the opposite of the intent.

## Defects reported upstream (R4)

Four issues filed with reproducible examples, workarounds and code suggestions —
see §8 of the analysis for the table and for two self-corrections I made while
verifying my own earlier claims.

## Verification

- `cargo test --test unit ci_cd::` — 131 passed. The workflow-invariant tests
  were updated for the new jobs rather than around them.
- `bash scripts/check-secrets.sh`, `bash scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` and
  `rust-script scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs --since main --until HEAD` all run
  clean locally.
- Regression test asserting the `mac.signIgnore` patterns match the browser
  runtime and not the app binary.
title: Fix CI/CD false positives and errors, and run every release check at the pull-request stage

body:
## Summary

Closes #895 (epic #710). CI produced an LCOV file, uploaded it, and never read the numbers — there was no threshold to fail and no way to notice a decrease. This makes the requirement real: coverage is measured, published, and ratcheted.

## What changed

**A non-decreasing ratchet.** `scripts/check-coverage-ratchet.rs` reads the LCOV report, compares each metric against the reviewed floor in `coverage/baseline.json`, and fails the build on a decrease beyond a stated tolerance. Raising a floor is automatic (`--update-baseline`). Lowering one is refused unless `--justification "<reviewed reason>"` is supplied, which is recorded in the baseline as `lowered_reason` — so a decrease reaches review as a sentence in the diff, not two digits changing.

**Published artifacts.** Each denominator emits a human-readable `coverage/summary-<name>.md` (per-metric table, deltas in percentage points, the ten least-covered files) into the run summary, plus a machine-readable `coverage/summary-<name>.json`. Both are uploaded as workflow artifacts with `if: always()`, so a failing run still publishes the numbers that explain the failure.

**Two honest denominators, never averaged.** A Rust percentage and a browser percentage count different things, and one combined number would let a large Rust suite mask an untested website. They are ratcheted separately:

| Denominator | Lines | Functions | Files |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Rust workspace | 86.47% | 44.34% | 408 |
| Browser production JavaScript | 50.48% | 45.54% | 40 |

**Browser coverage, which did not exist before.** `tests/web/` loads the unbundled `src/web/` page scripts and the 24-module worker mirror into a `node:vm` sandbox *under their real repository paths* — which is what makes V8 attribute coverage to the files the browser actually downloads — and boots the worker through its real entry point with the canonical `data/seed/*.lino` corpus behind `fetch`. 48 new tests, run by `npm run test:web` / `npm run coverage:web`.

**The denominator cannot be quietly narrowed.** `coverage/browser-unmeasured.txt` is a committed `path<TAB>reason` inventory of every `src/web/**` file the browser denominator does not measure. A file that is neither measured nor declared fails the build, as does a stale, redundant, or unexplained row. The list can shrink; it cannot grow silently.

**Coverage moved to its own workflow.** `.github/workflows/coverage.yml`, one job per denominator. Nothing in the release graph `needs:` these jobs, so the move changed no ordering; it also returns `release.yml` to 1930 lines, back under the 2000-line ceiling `scripts/check-file-size.rs` documents as debt that must not grow. The triggers, concurrency group, and change-detection gate match release.yml's contract, so a docs-only PR still does not pay for a 25-minute instrumented build.

## Tests

Regression tests for threshold enforcement and baseline updates, as the issue asks:

- **`scripts/check-coverage-ratchet-tests.rs`** — 30 cases run in CI via `rust-script --test scripts/check-coverage-ratchet.rs` in the `lint` job. They pin that a decrease fails, that an improvement only notices, that `--update-baseline` refuses to lower a floor without `--justification`, that an empty denominator is an error rather than a silent 0%, that a missing LCOV file is an error not a pass, that reports are written even when the ratchet breaks, and that the *committed* baseline is valid and carries a real measured floor for both denominators.
- **`tests/unit/ci-cd/workflow_coverage.rs`** — pins the workflow wiring: the gate's own tests run, each denominator is both enforced and published, timeouts and change-gating hold, and (issue #442) no job treats a *skipped* upstream check as a reason to run.

## Verification

Run locally on this branch, all green:

- `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features && cargo check --examples --all-features && rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs && rust-script scripts/check-hardcoded-language.rs`

Closes #674 (E55, parent #651; unblocks #708 and #699).

## Reproduction

Before this change, a freely phrased procedure such as:

> When I paste a link, fetch its title, translate it to Russian, save both, and reply with the translation.

could not be compiled, persisted, executed, and later explained as one inspectable program. The earlier PR draft also required callers to supply a learned operation manually, and Agent CLI stopped after artifact readback rather than executing it.

## What changed

- Generalized natural-language procedure compilation around shared intent formalization, ordered source-span decomposition, and seed-defined typed operations.
- Persisted one integrity-checked `compiled_procedure_artifact` that the solver, parser/interpreter, later explanation, in-repo Agent driver, public CLI, and external Agent CLI all reuse.
- Added evidence-driven learning: multilingual observations pair an unsupported surface with a successful seeded paraphrase; Formal AI infers the one canonical typed operation and rejects unknown or conflicting meanings.
- Kept learning fail-closed. Promotion requires en/ru/hi/zh parity, a named green regression suite, explicit human approval, and a content-addressed candidate whose inference evidence survives restart and is revalidated against tampering.
- Added `formal-ai procedure conformance`, which parses the persisted artifact and walks the generic `ProcedureHost` interpreter with a deterministic side-effect-free host.
- Advanced the Agent plan from write/readback to write, readback, public-command execution, exact execution-result verification, and an honest failure path.
- Preserved all-or-nothing compilation: an unsupported clause names the capability gap, records `skill_gap`, and emits no partial program.
- Refreshed closure and self-AST generated data, multilingual response seeds, architecture, requirements R501–R509, User Journey F2, and the issue case study.

## Agent CLI evidence

External `@link-assistant/agent` 0.25.3 session `ses_0559382b9ffeZg7gTXqS6kySQU` completed four Formal AI requests:

1. write the compiled artifact;
2. read the same bytes back;
3. execute `formal-ai procedure conformance` against that artifact;
4. return the verified `procedure_run` and source-cited steps.

- [Replay description](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-674-dfec7588a234/docs/case-studies/issue-674/agent-cli/README.md)
- [Raw Agent stream](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-674-dfec7588a234/docs/case-studies/issue-674/agent-cli/agent-stream.jsonl)

- [Deep analysis and root causes](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-674-dfec7588a234/dev/log/issues/674/pulls/815/analysis.md)

## CI/CD repair

Failed run 30328997145 was caused by `.github/workflows/release.yml` reaching 2,018 lines, above the repository’s 2,000-line hard limit. The five duplicated sccache setup blocks now use `.github/actions/setup-sccache/action.yml`; the workflow is 1,998 lines and its behavior is unchanged. Disk-policy coverage includes the new local action.

Desktop run 30398883119 then found a separate post-job failure: Windows x64 completed the cold release build, package smoke test, checksums, and artifact uploads in about 25 minutes, but `actions/cache` spent the remaining 3m40 compressing 194 MB of Cargo dependencies and was canceled at the 30-minute boundary. The desktop matrix now keeps the existing sccache compiler-output cache but does not register that redundant post-packaging Cargo archive. A workflow regression test pins this behavior.

The latest `main` is merged into this branch. Generated closure/self-AST conflicts were resolved by regeneration rather than manual combination.

## Summary

- Mine reusable operation sequences from three real recursive-core event logs with the existing held-out algorithm-discovery pipeline.
- Keep every proposal inert until canonical gates pass and a human explicitly runs `--apply --confirm`; promoted records remain data and never become executable handlers.
- Load the adopted seed into the method registry, retain rejected proposals with reasons, and replay the complete workflow in CI.
- Bound free-form evidence sampling so a large log cannot make repository validation exceed CI's job budget, while retaining exact metadata plus head and tail evidence.

## Root cause

Algorithm discovery could validate inert candidates, and promotion could replay trusted gates and materialize approved changes, but there was no bridge from real `EventLog` traces through those stages into the method registry. The registry also represented only compiled handlers, so it had no safe data-only representation for learned methods.

## Reproduction and verification

The new minimal regression test initially failed to compile because the event-log learning module and learned-method registry surface did not exist. It now proves that:

1. A repeated method is abstracted from two training logs and survives a held-out benchmark.
2. Discovery alone cannot change the registry.
3. Promotion requires canonical gate evidence plus explicit confirmation.
4. The adopted record is visible in the registry without becoming a dispatchable handler.
5. Failed candidates remain durable with suite-specific rejection reasons.
6. Localized event payloads in every registered language learn the same stable control-flow method.

Validated locally with:

- `cargo test --test unit issue_922_method_learning -- --nocapture`

## Summary

Fixes #1001 — the released container image `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai` is private, so anonymous `docker pull` fails with `unauthorized`, and nothing in the release pipeline ever noticed.

**Root cause (verified):** a container package created by a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push starts private, and it does not inherit the visibility of the repository it is linked to — only its access permissions. `.github/workflows/release.yml` pushed and moved on, so every release since the first push shipped an image no anonymous consumer could fetch, with a green build.

Live probe re-run while preparing this PR (no credentials):

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
    "https://ghcr.io/token?service=ghcr.io&scope=repository:link-assistant/formal-ai:pull"
401
```

401 = the package exists and is **private** (403 would mean absent, 200 public).

## Changes

- **`scripts/verify-ghcr-visibility.sh`** (new) — credential-free probe of GHCR's anonymous token endpoint. `200` passes; `401` fails with the manual remedy; `403` fails as "the push likely never happened"; transport errors and 5xx are retried (3 attempts, configurable) and then reported as *transient*, never as "private". The issued pull token is never printed, and the probe deliberately sends no credentials — authenticating would make a private package answer 200 and recreate exactly the false negative being closed. Following the issue #977 convention, one script is shared by both release paths.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — the verification step runs immediately after the GHCR push in **both** `auto-release` and `manual-release`, under the same `if:` condition as the push it verifies.
- **`README.md`** — how to tell a private package from a missing one, and the two workarounds (`docker login ghcr.io` with `read:packages`, or `cargo install formal-ai --locked`) until the package is made public.
- **`tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1001.rs`** (new, 10 tests) — one test per requirement plus workflow-level whole-task coverage.

## Reproduction and verification

Reproduction is the `401` above; the automated test reproduces it hermetically with a fake `curl` on `PATH` (the `scripts/install-node-dependencies.sh` sandbox pattern from issue #796), so no network is touched:

```
$ cargo test --test unit --all-features ci_cd::issue_1001
running 10 tests ... test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed
```

Covered: public passes (and no retry, and no token in the log); private fails with `PRIVATE` + "Change visibility"; absent fails with `DENIED` and is *not* called private; 503 is retried 3× and reported as transient; an unexpected status fails loudly instead of passing by default; an unset `GHCR_IMAGE` is not silent success; the probe scope strips the `ghcr.io/` host and any `:tag` / `@digest`; the script contains no credential plumbing; both release jobs call the script after the push with the push's own condition; the script parses under `bash -n`.

Every assertion fails against the pre-fix pipeline. Local CI (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features`, full `ci_cd` suite — 193 tests) is green.

## What this PR cannot do

- **Making the package public is manual.** Package visibility is not settable through the REST API ([community discussion #33310](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/33310)): package page → *Package settings* → *Danger Zone* → *Change visibility* → *Public*. **@konard**, this one-off step is still needed — until it is done, the new gate will (correctly) fail the next release.
- **The Docker Hub mirror is a repository-variable setting.** `scripts/configure-dockerhub-publishing.sh` already publishes a mirror whenever `DOCKERHUB_IMAGE` is set; setting that variable is a repository-settings action, not a code change.
title: fix(ci): fail the release when the GHCR image is not anonymously pullable

Fixes https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/932

## Summary

- declare the language → `link-foundation/box` image mapping and the traditional init commands as data in `data/meta/box-language-projects.lino`, read by Rust, by both shell scripts and by the CI-matrix invariant test
- generate the project corpus out of the solver itself — the program from English, Russian, Hindi and Chinese prompts, the init script from the contract's own README steps — and build and run it inside the matching image
- add a `box-language-projects` CI matrix leg, one runner per language, gated like the other slow legs
- expose the same check from `cargo test`, skipping gracefully when Docker is unavailable
- fix the routing defect the corpus exposed: install guides that name project creation were answered by the software-project planner

This is the part of PR #119 that was never delivered. The maintainer asked to "*test each software project of a specific language inside such version of link foundation box docker image, that matches the language*" and to "*use traditional commands to init repositories for each language*"; no CI leg has ever done that.

## Reproduction

Building the corpus surfaced a dispatch bug. Asking for the Go installation guide as a shell script — the exact prompt the generator issues — answered with a software-project *plan*:

```
  left: "software_project_plan"
 right: "installation_conversion"
test installation_conversion::go_module_install_guide_converts_to_a_script ... FAILED
```

The complete pre-fix output is preserved in `docs/case-studies/issue-932/raw-data/repro-before.log`, captured by reverting the promotion gate this PR adds.

`data/seed/handler-precedence.lino` already ranks `installation_conversion` (42) ahead of `software_project` (46), but `MethodRegistry::ordered_method_names_for_relevants` hoists *any* method named by a `handler:<name>` relevant ahead of the whole precedence table. The promotion array emitted `handler:software_project` and `handler:write_script` and never `handler:installation_conversion`, so a guide whose steps say "create the project" and "build the project" matched the promoted cues and the declared precedence never applied. The array also moved to `src/intent_formalization/prompt_relevants.rs`: the parent module was at 897 of its reviewed 900-line ceiling.

## Design

`data/meta/box-language-projects.lino` is the single contract — registry, namespace, image tag, project directory, expected output, the four prompt locales, and one record per language carrying its image, program file, code fence, optional shell prelude, whether the init needs network, and the ordered traditional init steps.

`scripts/generate-box-language-corpus.sh` asks the solver for the program once per locale and refuses to continue unless the four answers are byte-identical, rebuilds the installation guide from the contract's init steps, asks the solver to convert that guide into a shell script, and asserts every declared command survives the conversion. `scripts/verify-box-language-projects.sh` streams the corpus into `docker run` as a `tar` stream (bind mounts would land root-owned host files or mismatch the container's `box` uid) and runs `scripts/run-box-language-project.sh` inside the image, which fails unless the init script exits zero, the project directory exists and the program prints `Hello, world!`. Legs whose init needs no network run with `--network none`.

`data/meta/box-image-survey.lino` records the Docker Hub survey: six per-language variants exist under `konard` (`box-rust`, `box-python`, `box-js`, `box-go`, `box-java`, `box-ruby`), all publishing `2.4.0`, which is therefore the pinned tag — `latest` was rejected because the check must not change meaning between two runs of the same commit. `konard/box-c`, `box-cpp`, `box-csharp` and `box-dotnet` do not exist, so C, C++ and C# are recorded as deferred records naming the full `konard/box` image they wait for, instead of being silently dropped. `every_matrix_image_was_actually_found_on_the_registry` fails if the matrix ever names an image the survey did not find.

The images are 4.21–7.81 GB, so no single runner holds several of them next to a cargo build. That is why the CI leg is a matrix — one image per runner — and why it frees runner disk first.

## Verification

Every language was built and run by hand inside its image before CI was trusted; the logs are `docs/case-studies/issue-932/raw-data/verify-<language>.log`:

```
ok: rust project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-rust:2.4.0
ok: python project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-python:2.4.0
ok: javascript project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-js:2.4.0
ok: typescript project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-js:2.4.0
ok: go project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-go:2.4.0
ok: java project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-java:2.4.0
ok: ruby project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-ruby:2.4.0
```

- `cargo test --test unit` — 2745 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --test unit -- ci_cd::issue_999 issue_673_self_ast_census issue_918 ci_cd::issue_932 issue_932 installation_conversion` — 49 passed, re-run after merging `main`
- `cargo test --doc`, `cargo check --examples --all-features`
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features` — clean
- `shellcheck` (via `koalaman/shellcheck:stable`) on all four new and edited scripts — clean

A repository-wide parallel run also produced 18 integration failures, all `Os { code: 11, kind: WouldBlock }` while opening sockets on a loaded 6-core box. All 24 of those tests pass when rerun with `--test-threads=2` (`ci-logs/integration-rerun.log`), so they are runner resource exhaustion, not regressions. Fresh GitHub Actions at the final pushed SHA provide the clean sharded verification.

This is a CI and container change, not visual UI work, so before/after screenshots and visual regression tests do not apply.

## Self-hosting and evidence

The real Formal AI Agent CLI authored one of the five smallest implementation leaves: the box image survey. Session `ses_fffb7e760ffeebqPgLR1KV1DK5`, the server log, the CLI log, the decomposition and the byte-identical artifact are preserved under `docs/case-studies/issue-932/self-hosting-authorship/`, and `tests/unit/issue_932_self_authoring.rs` fails if the committed `data/meta/box-image-survey.lino` ever stops matching the captured artifact. `experiments/issue_932_self_authoring/run.sh` reproduces the session.

The issue case study, requirement matrix (R932-1 … R932-13), image survey and raw GitHub evidence are under `docs/case-studies/issue-932/` and `docs/requirements/issue-0932-box-language-projects.md`.

## Summary

- make the macOS packaging retry log genuinely unique under BSD `mktemp`, and align the proxy-log assertion with the product's canonical path
- centralize BSD/util-linux `script(1)` PTY launch syntax, guard empty Bash arrays under stock macOS Bash 3.2, and restore a full `macos-15-intel` test leg
- make the shared runner-disk bootstrap use POSIX `df -Pk`, after the first fresh macOS job exposed its GNU-only `--output=avail` flag
- wait for the fake interactive client before writing and defer PTY EOF until command exit, after macOS exposed both lifecycle races
- add per-requirement and whole-task regressions, issue/PR case studies, and real Formal AI / Agent CLI authorship evidence

## Root causes

The Linux-only test matrix hid four independent platform assumptions: a suffix after `mktemp`'s placeholder, a raw-vs-canonical path comparison, util-linux-only PTY flags, and an unguarded empty-array expansion under Bash 3.2 nounset semantics. The first new macOS job also exposed GNU-only `df --output=avail` in its pre-test disk cleanup; that helper now uses the POSIX `df -Pk` columns. Two later jobs exposed both halves of an interactive-test race: BSD `script` could deliver terminal EOF before the fake client started reading, and closing its input immediately after a write could translate that close into EOT ahead of the buffered line. The PTY helper now waits for a line-ending-independent readiness marker, sends input, and retains stdin until the command exits.

## Tests

- `cargo test --test issue_961_macos_portability -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test --test issue_757_session_files -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test --test unit macos_package_retry -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test --test integration pty:: -- --nocapture`
- both affected PTY integration tests
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast --verbose`
- formatting, Clippy, example checking, and repository integrity scripts

The tests-first issue contract failed all five original assertions before the implementation. After the first pushed macOS job failed before Cargo, two additional tests reproduced its BSD `df` error. The next jobs exposed the PTY readiness and early-EOF races; each received a failing regression before its repair. The complete issue contract is now 12/12 and the shared PTY helper suite is 4/4. The original macOS audit's six failing cases and the post-fix evidence are documented in the case study.

Final SHA `9fa69dfc` passed the complete [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/31396066284), including `Test (ubuntu-latest)` and `Test (macos-15-intel)`. Closes #842.

## Summary

- Turns the issue #840 dataset into a strict, appendable 24-node quality ratchet for reports #838, #827, and #826.
- Fixes the two false greens exposed by stronger judging: multilingual definition-example requests now share one slot-driven route, and an isolated contextual pronoun asks for its missing antecedent instead of searching the web.
- Filters flattened web evidence by language-independent sentence structure so navigation fragments and adjacent headings are not repeated as an answer.
- Separates assistant-authored claims from raw tool evidence and judges positive assertions, alternatives, refusals, capability menus, tool routes, and shell-command shape.
- Derives evidence-bearing failure-learning proposals on every run while keeping promotion explicitly human-gated.
- Runs the full stable-ID ratchet in its own bounded, least-privilege CI workflow and retains both measurements and learning proposals.
- Pins sccache 0.16.0 after the newly released 0.17.0 expanded Rust response files past the Windows command-line limit; workflow regression coverage prevents another silent tool-version upgrade.

## Measured outcome

The historical v0.303.0 baseline passed **8/24**. The final strict measurement passes **24/24**:

| Slice | Historical | Final |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total | 8/24 | **24/24** |
| L1 — original requests | 1/3 | **3/3** |
| L2 | 1/6 | **6/6** |
| L3 | 2/7 | **7/7** |
| L4 — atomic subtasks | 4/8 | **8/8** |
| #838 local discovery | 3/10 | **10/10** |
| #827 definition/follow-up | 1/7 | **7/7** |
| #826 comparison/report | 4/7 | **7/7** |

L1 and L4 now both pass at 100%, removing the reported composition/decomposition inversion.

## Root cause and generalized production rules

The earlier harness allowed raw tool output to satisfy answer assertions and did not require positive answer evidence or route parity on every node. Re-judging the existing responses exposed two real failures:

- `827.L4.a` returned the generic Russian unknown fallback because “give an example of X” had no agentic research route.
- `827.L4.b` searched the public web for the pronoun `это` even though the request supplied no antecedent.

Regression tests were added first. The production fix is structural:

- `definition_example_request` is one slotted meaning role. English and Russian use prefix slots, Hindi uses a suffix slot, and Chinese uses a circumfix slot. The planner extracts the subject from slot structure, so another language or phrasing is a seed-data extension rather than a prompt-specific Rust branch.
- A parsed concept query whose subject is a non-referential pronoun and whose only context is a sentence returns the existing localized clarification.
- Fetched evidence prefers complete prose blocks identified by script-level sentence terminals. If no complete block exists, the ordinary relevance path retains all evidence, preserving terse legitimate answers without a provider-specific phrase blocklist.

Focused Rust coverage is in `tests/unit/issue_842.rs`.

## A falsifiable, growing ladder

`experiments/issue_840_task_ladder/ladder.py` now records and judges:

- assistant output independently from the complete tool transcript;
- `expect`, `expect_any`, and `forbid` answer assertions;
- required and forbidden tool routes;
- forbidden command fragments;
- execution errors, exact generic refusals, and capability-menu fallbacks.

The offline web fixture deliberately includes page controls and adjacent headings. Those strings are forbidden in answers, so successful routing alone cannot masquerade as synthesis.

The baseline comparison is per stable task ID. It rejects a removed node, a previously green node that regresses, or any failing appended node. New maintainer reports extend the graph with new IDs and can advance `results.json` only after all old and new nodes pass.

Every failed observation also becomes a proposal containing its stable ID, prompt, assistant output, tools, commands, error, and exact violated assertions. Proposals remain `awaiting_human_review`; the harness cannot promote behavior or move the baseline itself.

## Real clients and Formal AI self-application

The final release binary passed the representative OpenCode TUI node and the complete real Agent CLI journeys for local discovery, definition/follow-up research, comparison, and Russian report creation.

The reviewed issue decomposition names five smallest leaves. Formal AI, through the real Agent CLI, authored and verified the durable stable-ID invariant leaf (**1/5 = 20%**); the other four remain honestly attributed to human tool extension. Session `ses_052c4f066ffecNc3GC3Dk13wJ9` and its raw stream, server trace, decomposition, and byte-identical artifact are retained under `docs/case-studies/issue-842/self-hosting/`.

Final-source Agent CLI sessions `ses_052984123ffenzPVkmsVADtAHL` and `ses_0528b8463ffeTZ6UPSJy5tLHmI` refreshed the self-AST and self-healing axes. The deterministic renderer then expanded the live slice to all **330 owned-source documents / 13,160 Links Notation lines**. Canonical and evidence snapshots are byte-identical, and the self-hosting release ratchet holds against `origin/main`.

The complete rationale and reproducible evidence map are in `docs/case-studies/issue-842/README.md`.

## Verification

Passing locally on final commit `8443ed65bc23a398772770397a0157fa1075c576`:

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check --examples --all-features`
- `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs`
- `rust-script scripts/check-hardcoded-language.rs`
- `GITHUB_BASE_REF=main npm --prefix tests/e2e run check:language-test-coverage` — **en, ru, hi, zh**
- `python3 -m unittest -v experiments/issue_840_task_ladder/test_ladder.py` — **9/9**
- task-ladder workflow contract tests — **5/5**
- release-workflow tests — **25/25**, including the pinned sccache regression
- `cargo test --lib --bins --tests --all-features --verbose` — all targets green; primary unit target **2,162 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored**
- Rust doctests — green
- strict stable-ID task ladder — **24/24**, zero learning candidates
- reference-agent differential gate — **24/24**, 2 commands versus the best reference's 5
- final real Agent CLI E2E — all four seed journeys passed

Fresh GitHub Actions verification for the exact final SHA:

| Workflow | Result |
| --- | --- |
| [Task Ladder](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/30448420040) | **Passed** — strict 24/24 ratchet |
| [External Benchmarks](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/30448420028) | **Passed** |
| [Agentic CLI Matrix](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/30448420075) | **Passed** |
| [Desktop Release](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/30448420055) | **Passed** — all six OS/architecture builds and VSIX packaging; a failed-job rerun confirmed the first macOS ARM `hdiutil` device error was runner-transient |
| [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/30448420084) | **Passed** |

To reproduce the committed gate:

```bash
cargo build --release --bin formal-ai
BASELINE=experiments/issue_840_task_ladder/results.json \
  OUT=/tmp/issue842-results.json \
  LEARNING_OUT=/tmp/issue842-learning.json \
  experiments/issue_840_task_ladder/run_ladder.sh
```

No visual UI changed, so before/after screenshots are not applicable.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Baseline rises from 8/24 to 24/24.
- [x] L1 performs at least as well as L4: both are 100%.
- [x] Equivalent local-search phrasings route identically.
- [x] No node passes through a capability menu or generic refusal.
- [x] CI runs the strict ladder, records its score, and retains evidence.
- [x] Assertions cover assistant claims, routes, commands, and synthesis leakage.
- [x] Deterministic web-fixture and real-client variants both pass.
- [x] New reports have an executable stable-ID extension and review-gated learning protocol.

## Summary

- add bounded, deterministic e-graph equality saturation behind the optional `equality-saturation` feature
- add native bounded, range-restricted, function-free positive Datalog inference
- adapt pinned egg and Ascent Rust sources into the external benchmark harness and grade proof status from canonical structured LiNo traces
- record honest 2026-08-14 scores on formal-ai 0.343.0: egg 20/20 and Ascent 5/5
- preserve issue, upstream-license, benchmark, and real Agent CLI evidence in `docs/case-studies/issue-923/`

Fixes #923.

## Reproduction and root cause

Before this change the symbolic kernel could decide propositional SAT and linear arithmetic, but it had no general path for equivalence modulo rewrite laws or recursive relational consequences. The benchmark harness also had no Rust-source adapter or strict proof-status grading, so those missing capabilities could not be measured honestly against external cases.

Focused regressions reproduce both gaps with the non-numeric identity `(+ x 0) = x` and transitive reachability from `edge(a,b)` plus `edge(b,c)`. They also pin the prior infix-linear dispatch path and prove that search misses, unsafe rules, and resource ceilings remain inconclusive rather than becoming false disproofs.

## Implementation

- `egg` 0.11.0 is MIT licensed, optional, uses default features off, and enables deterministic behavior only. Saturation is bounded to 12 iterations and 20,000 e-graph nodes.
- Datalog evaluation is implemented in-tree with ceilings of 512 clauses, arity 16, 10,000 facts, 100,000 join substitutions, and 256 rounds.
- The external adapter pins egg commit `2f31b28e3f9d78e02273b6c6d4201b5b0720b343` and Ascent commit `cf5e9a87525bb95268cf6680a59882264b0fe0de`.
- The proof grader parses canonical indented LiNo and accepts only exact structured `proof_outcome` events; prose and prefix/suffix forgeries are rejected.
- Decision conclusions are seed-backed for every registered locale. The new records live in the bounded `multilingual-responses-symbolic.lino` shard.
- The latest `main` (formal-ai 0.343.0) is merged. Two behavior-preserving `const`/`fmt::Write` cleanups keep its #991 examples warning-free on Rust 1.96.

## Honest external scores

| Suite | Upstream cases | Passed | Failed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| egg math rewrite laws | 20 | 20 | 0 |
| Ascent transitive closure | 5 | 5 | 0 |

Commands rerun on the final 0.343.0 tree:

```text
cargo run --all-features --bin formal-ai -- benchmark run --suite egg_math --slice 20
cargo run --all-features --bin formal-ai -- benchmark run --suite ascent_transitive_closure --slice 5
```

## Verification

- focused issue suite: 11 passed, 1 deliberately ignored live test
- pinned upstream live test: 1 passed
- all-feature serial integration suite: 342 passed, 1 ignored
- final source suite: 487 passed
- final unit suite: 2,741 passed, 4 ignored
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check --no-default-features`
- registered `web` and `wasm` stages; worker 291,531 bytes against the 524,288-byte ceiling
- derived-artifact regeneration: 470 self-AST documents, 0 rewrites/removals on the final rerun

The post-merge catalog-size regressions were reproduced before the new symbolic responses were moved into their own registered shard; both size tests pass after the split. No UI behavior changed, so screenshots are not applicable.

## Self-hosting evidence

Real Agent CLI session `ses_001f733ceffe5UboLW4JATfkoZ` authored one reviewed leaf. Its raw stream, server log, task, session id, exact output, and worktree status are committed under `docs/case-studies/issue-923/agent-cli-evidence/` and linked by commit trailers.

## Summary

- Audits Formal AI's current legal/compliance posture and records the truthful
  starting state: this repository ships symbolic software, not trained neural
  weights, and has no approved training or distillation sources.
- Adds a conservative, fail-closed
  [legal/compliance policy](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-834-14f41fd75c97/LEGAL-COMPLIANCE.md)
  covering public-domain contributions, third-party rights, closed APIs,
  personal data, prohibited uses, the EU AI Act, regional review triggers, and
  warranty limits.
- Adds a canonical
  [training-source registry](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-834-14f41fd75c97/data/training/source-registry.json),
  source-review form, and executable equality gate. Every future
  parameter-updating artifact must have an approved, non-empty 43-field record;
  undocumented artifacts fail CI.
- Tightens the contribution guide and PR template against leaked/proprietary
  code, unauthorized paid/access-controlled data, large copyrighted payloads,
  secrets, and real personal data.
- Answers the issue's Llama 3.3, Mistral 7B, OpenRouter, and regional-law
  questions using exact-version, provider-route, and primary-source analysis.

## Audit result

The repository had useful isolated controls—the Unlicense, benchmark
provenance, runtime-source records, and personal-event-log boundaries—but no
inbound public-domain submission rule and no enforceable training-source
intake. This change closes that engineering gap without claiming worldwide
legal clearance.

Benchmark fixtures, runtime retrieval/cache data, and community examples are
now explicitly separate from training data. Changing their purpose requires a
new review. The empty registry is paired with
`current_state: "no-approved-training-sources"` and an exact recursive
artifact/registry comparison, so it cannot be treated as implicit approval.

The full findings, before/after matrix, primary research, and residual counsel
boundary are preserved in the
[issue #834 case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-834-14f41fd75c97/docs/case-studies/issue-834/README.md).

## Reproduction and verification

The ten new regressions were run before implementation and all failed on the
missing controls:

- [reproduction-before.log](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-834-14f41fd75c97/docs/case-studies/issue-834/test-logs/reproduction-before.log)

After implementation:

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --all-features --test unit docs_requirements_issue_834 -- --test-threads=1
cargo test --all-features --test unit specification::self_hosting_metric -- --test-threads=1
cargo test --all-features --test unit ci_cd::workflow_release -- --test-threads=1
cargo test --all-features --verbose
rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs
rust-script scripts/check-hardcoded-language.rs
```

Results:

- issue-specific regressions: 10 passed, 0 failed;
- self-hosting metric regressions: 8 passed, 0 failed;
- release-workflow regressions: 24 passed, 0 failed;
- binary tests: 188 passed, 0 failed;
- integration tests: 481 passed, 0 failed;
- unit tests: 2,002 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored by their existing declarations;
- doc tests: passed;
- formatting, Clippy, file-size policy, and hardcoded-language policy: passed.

The verbose suite reported several existing agent-replay and ratchet tests after
60 seconds; every reported test completed successfully. Logs are retained in
[`docs/case-studies/issue-834/test-logs/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-834-14f41fd75c97/docs/case-studies/issue-834/test-logs).

## Hosted CI hardening

The first hosted run proved that the self-hosting evidence passes, then its
test runner exhausted `/` after restoring the target-heavy Cargo cache. The
failure reproduced on two separate hosted runners: first the runner worker
could not write its diagnostic log, then `rustc` could not create a temporary
directory and the linker terminated with `SIGBUS`.

A focused workflow regression now requires the test job to run the repository's
existing hosted-runner disk cleanup before restoring that cache. The minimal
workflow change reuses `scripts/free-runner-disk.sh`, which is already used by
the repository's other heavy build jobs.

The replacement
[CI/CD Pipeline run](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/30088957035)
passed every check at head `0a144925`. On the test runner, cleanup reduced root
usage from 58 GiB to 38 GiB and increased free space from 88 GiB to 107 GiB
before cache restoration. The full test job then passed in 18m40s.

## Formal AI evidence and self-hosting ratchet

The initial external `solve` wrapper rejected its configured `formal-ai` model
before a session began. That failure remains preserved honestly in the case
study, and the manually authored legal audit and tests carry no self-authorship
trailers.

After CI reproduced the branch-local self-hosting failure at 0.00% (0/1,325
changed lines), the established isolated local Agent CLI path ran a real Formal
AI session, `ses_06c5ab43dffekcO0P7PW77UVcL`. It created a representative
source-links artifact and an exhaustive two-shard projection covering all 293
owned modules. The generator verified every source-to-links-to-source round
trip byte-for-byte.

The transcript and artifacts are preserved in
[`self-hosting-evidence/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-834-14f41fd75c97/docs/case-studies/issue-834/self-hosting-evidence).
Only the isolated generated-artifact commit carries the paired
`Formal-AI-Session` and `Formal-AI-Evidence` trailers; the legal work remains
unattributed.

Local differential result at head `0a144925`:

```text
61.04% (2168/3552 changed lines; 1/13 commits)
self-hosting ratchet holds against origin/main
```

Closes #834

## Summary

- route explicit local filesystem discovery requests through a seed-defined `find` command before shared capability and web-search routing
- distinguish Desktop, home/computer, and current-directory scopes, plus file/folder predicates, across English, Russian, Hindi, and Chinese
- generate safe fuzzy filename patterns for natural names such as `hive-mind-control center`, while preserving open-web `find` requests as web searches
- cover the OpenAI Chat/Responses and Anthropic protocol surfaces used by Agent, OpenCode, Codex, and Claude
- add a real four-client E2E harness and an OpenCode TUI transcript verifier based on `link-foundation/command-stream`
- make the existing meaning-detail Agent E2Es hermetic with a repository-owned MCP search/fetch fixture, preserving the complete five-turn recipe without depending on Exa availability
- keep every Agent scenario inside the required gate local by disabling hosted session summarization job-wide and routing the remaining research harnesses through deterministic MCP evidence
- add a 56-case Formal-AI-authored benchmark spanning the supported actions, scopes, kinds, and languages
- preserve the investigation, self-authored requirements, raw dialogs, TUI frames, benchmark sessions, test logs, and changelog fragment

Fixes #819.

## Reproduction and result

Before this change, the reported prompt:

```text
Find hive-mind-control center folder on my desktop
```

fell through to `websearch`. The regression test first pinned that failure and now verifies a single local command equivalent to:

```sh
find "${FORMAL_AI_DESKTOP_DIR:-$HOME/Desktop}" -type d \( -iname '*hive*mind*control*center*' ... \) -print -quit
```

Against an isolated Desktop fixture, that command returns `Desktop/Archive/hive-control-center`. No web tool is called. Open-web requests such as “Find information online…” remain routed to `websearch`.

## Generalization benchmark

Formal AI authored a 56-case benchmark partitioned across English, Russian, Hindi, and Chinese. It exhausts seeded action/scope/kind combinations for Desktop, home/computer, and current-directory lookup while asserting `bash`/`find` and prohibiting `websearch`.

Running the benchmark uncovered a second-order bug: the word “directory” inside a current-directory scope could incorrectly force `-type d` for a requested document. The implementation now removes the matched action and complete scope phrase before classifying file/folder kind, and all 56 cases pass.

## CI reliability

The original failing `E2E Tests (agent CLI ↔ formal-ai)` job never reached the issue-819 scenario: Agent's built-in `websearch` failed in the earlier tomato and potato meaning-detail scenarios with `AI_APICallError: No provider available`. Those scenarios now configure a local, read-only MCP fixture backed by the repository's committed Wikidata lexeme cache. Agent still performs distinct search and fetch tool calls, but the required gate no longer depends on a hosted Exa provider.

A fresh run confirmed both meaning-detail steps green, then exposed the same dependency class in Agent's automatic `opencode/big-pickle` session summarizer during the diagram recipe. The shared harness now also passes `--no-summarize-session --compaction-model same`, following the repository's established Agent invocation pattern, so no hosted model is called between local tool turns.

The next fresh run passed the diagram and every scenario through issue #730, then found that issue #758 invokes Agent directly and could still start the hosted summarizer. The Agent E2E job now sets `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_SUMMARIZE_SESSION=false`, covering shared and issue-specific invocations alike. A complete harness audit also found two later scenarios that still used Agent's hosted Exa tools: issues #687 and #771 now use the repository's deterministic research MCP, while preserving real namespaced search/fetch execution and issue #771's oversized-page regression.

That full Agent gate passed, while the independent self-hosting ratchet rejected the first 165-line form of the final hardening commit because the Codex-authored work was correctly unattributed. The same behavior and regression were compacted to 135 measured lines instead of claiming false `Formal-AI-*` trailers; `scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs --check-ratchet origin/main --until HEAD` now passes.

## Verification

- `cargo test --all-features --verbose` — all integration groups and doctests pass; main unit corpus plus focused CI regressions: 1,962 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `rust-script scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs --check-ratchet origin/main --until HEAD`
- both normal and docs.rs-style `cargo doc` profiles with `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`
- native release and WASM worker builds, including the WASM size gate
- generated self-AST drift, total closure, self-hosting-ratchet, file-size, hardcoded-language, i18n, language-parity, language-coverage, intent-coverage, web-TDZ, web hardcoded-UI, VS Code, and desktop checks
- issue #819 unit tests exhaust every seeded action/scope/kind phrase, run all 56 benchmark cases, and execute the generated command against a real isolated fixture
- protocol integration tests cover Agent/OpenCode Chat Completions, Claude Anthropic Messages, and Codex Responses schemas
- real Agent meaning-detail runs pass with exact `search -> fetch -> write -> verify -> final` traces through the local MCP fixture for both tomato and potato
- real Agent issue #687, #771, and #781 research E2Es pass through the local MCP; issue #771 fetches the deterministic oversized page before filing its bounded report
- release-binary E2E passes for real Agent, OpenCode, Claude, and Codex CLIs with the complete `user -> find -> tool result -> final answer` sequence
- real OpenCode TUI capture passes frame deduplication and full dialog-structure verification through `command-stream`

## Evidence

- [Issue #819 case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-819-ebe5e6322d6c/docs/case-studies/issue-819)
- [56-case benchmark manifest](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-819-ebe5e6322d6c/data/benchmarks/local-path-discovery-suite.lino)
- [Four-client and TUI run](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-819-ebe5e6322d6c/docs/case-studies/issue-819/raw-data/e2e/four-client-and-tui.log)
- [Deduplicated OpenCode TUI transcript](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-819-ebe5e6322d6c/docs/case-studies/issue-819/raw-data/e2e/opencode-tui/tui-transcript.json)
- [Requirements trace](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-819-ebe5e6322d6c/docs/case-studies/issue-819/requirements.md)
- [Self-authoring evidence](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-819-ebe5e6322d6c/docs/case-studies/issue-819/raw-data/self-authoring)

This is behavioral routing and test-infrastructure work rather than a visual UI change, so there is no before/after screenshot; the committed TUI frames are the relevant UI evidence.

## Summary

- attest desktop and VS Code artifacts by direct path, removing the released `actions/attest@v4` host-EOL checksum parser from the Windows provenance path
- make rustdoc warnings fatal and repair all 61 broken/intra-doc-link warnings that the former workflow silently accepted
- default both workflows to read-only permissions, elevate publisher jobs explicitly, and bound every desktop job with a timeout
- classify only the exact reviewed npm/action dependency diagnostics, with upstream links, while failing closed on every new warning
- prevent Agent CLI file-authoring requests that mention an existing issue from creating duplicate GitHub issues; add multilingual regressions and a real Agent CLI E2E
- repair release-generated changelog whitespace and the missing issue 716 fragment-release provenance row
- preserve complete CI logs, API records, template trees/diffs, upstream research, red/green reproductions, and real Agent CLI streams in `docs/case-studies/issue-730/`

Closes #730.

## Root causes and reproduction

Desktop run 29465138404 failed on both Windows architectures. The released v4 bundle still executes `checksums.split(os.EOL)`; its latest v4.1.1 release predates the merged `/\r?\n/` fix in actions/attest#443. An LF manifest therefore became one oversized subject on Windows. Both attestation sites now pass the artifacts themselves through `subject-path`; portable checksum files remain release assets but are no longer executable selectors.

The successful main run 29463393707 also exposed a false green: `RUSTFLAGS` did not configure rustdoc and the job deliberately left `RUSTDOCFLAGS` unset. `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` reproduced 61 warnings before the fix and passes after all links are corrected.

Self-hosting through the real Agent CLI exposed a separate report-router defect: file/workflow requests containing “issue 730” were interpreted as `gh issue create`. The router now requires the report action to govern a nearby issue/repository subject; ambiguous file-writing verbs require natural word order. The vocabulary remains seed-backed and production code contains no issue-specific prompt.

## Verification

- Final-sha [CI/CD Pipeline run 29483282520](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29483282520) passed every required job on `e4f77d61be6a765c9b976628e6ff24e9c04438c6`; it had no failed steps or error annotations. Its two notices and two sub-limit file-size warnings are classified in the case study.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

## Summary

- replace the deprecated provenance wrapper with `actions/attest@v4`, fixing LF-only checksum parsing on Windows x64 and arm64
- always retain `lcov.info` as a workflow artifact and run Codecov v7 fail-closed when its token is configured
- update artifact-download, configure deterministic Git initialization, package the VSIX license, and downgrade the intentional ad-hoc signing fallback from a warning to a notice
- keep hard file-size limits repository-wide while limiting warning-band annotations to files changed by the triggering event
- compare the complete PR/push range so a docs-only final commit cannot hide earlier code changes and skip required CI jobs
- make Formal AI's edit planner read the target before editing so Agent CLI read-before-write enforcement can execute the patch
- classify the two exact Agent CLI 0.25.0 diagnostics into one linked notice while failing on any new dependency stderr
- retain the complete CI/template audit, raw logs, alternatives, upstream research, and Agent CLI traces in `docs/case-studies/issue-717/`

Closes #717.

## Root cause and reproduction

Desktop release run 29354019108 generated LF-only checksum manifests, then `actions/attest-build-provenance@v2` split them using Windows `os.EOL` (CRLF). The whole manifest became one subject name and GitHub rejected it for exceeding 256 characters. This is the same defect as [actions/attest#440](https://github.com/actions/attest/issues/440), fixed by [actions/attest#443](https://github.com/actions/attest/pull/443) and released in v4.

The pre-fix policy regression is preserved in `docs/case-studies/issue-717/raw-data/regression-before-fix.log`. It failed all affected assertions before the workflow edits. Both checksum attestation sites are now covered.

The first post-push run reproduced a change-detection false negative: it compared only the final docs commit and skipped Rust tests/coverage despite earlier Rust commits in the PR. The detector now compares the synthetic PR merge parents, or `github.event.before..HEAD` for a push, with behavior tests for both event types.

The next complete run exposed a second false green: Codecov rejected its tokenless upload but `fail_ci_if_error: false` left the coverage job successful. A follow-up run proved GitHub could issue an OIDC token but Codecov had not provisioned this repository. Coverage is now always retained as a workflow artifact; a configured Codecov upload uses its repository token and fails on delivery errors, while an unconfigured integration emits one explicit notice. That run also exposed repeated Agent CLI dependency warnings; [link-assistant/agent#279](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/279) tracks the owning call sites.

## Verification

- final CI on the latest merged `main`: [run 29395706981](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29395706981) — all required jobs passed
- `cargo test --all-features --verbose` after merging the latest `main`: 1,601 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored; doc tests passed

- desktop unit and smoke tests: 102 passed

The full result, exact commands, logs, run timeline, alternatives, and requirements traceability are in [`docs/case-studies/issue-717/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-717-bccddb8af16e/docs/case-studies/issue-717/README.md).

## Upstream follow-ups
