Closes #894 (child of #710).

The 2026-06-14 four-template CI/CD audit (`docs/case-studies/issue-479/template-comparison/REPORT.md`) ended with *drafted* upstream issues — "Title:", "Body:", "Check:" — and no field in which a filing URL could live. A recommendation with no URL is indistinguishable from an unreported gap and, once the templates move on, from a gap that no longer exists. Two months later four of the report's eight working-repo recommendations had in fact been closed downstream, with no record of it anywhere. Nothing in CI could catch that, because no test read the report.

## What this PR does

**1. Revalidation.** Every finding was re-checked against the current template default branches — `js` `7b70923`, `rust` `c867f78`, `python` `98d6dca`, `csharp` `6806bd9`, all fetched 2026-08-05 — and against the working repo's current `release.yml`. Commands and verbatim output are preserved in `docs/case-studies/issue-894/raw-data/revalidation-greps.txt` and `revalidation-greps-2.txt`.

**2. Filing.** Eight issues filed upstream, each with a reproduction, a workaround and a concrete suggested fix:

| ID | Gap | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| U1-js / U1-rust / U1-python / U1-csharp | No CI security scanning (CodeQL for code *and* GitHub Actions workflows, `dependency-review-action`) | link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#122, link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#115, link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#48, link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#43 |
| U2-rust / U2-python / U2-csharp | No broken-link checker; `links.yml` exists only in the JS template | link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#116, link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#49, link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#44 |
| U3-rust | No desktop-release workflow / `/download` page — ships the fixed #479 `workflow_run.head_sha` resolver and the electron-builder 26 `mac.identity=-` ad-hoc signing flag as prior art | link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#117 |

All eight bodies are preserved verbatim under `docs/case-studies/issue-894/raw-data/` (`sec-*.md`, `links-*.md`, `desktop-rust.md`), and the created-issue metadata in `filed-upstream-issues.json`.

**3. Ledger.** The report's *Recommended upstream issues to file* section is replaced by *Upstream filing status (revalidated 2026-08-05)*, keyed by finding ID with an explicit status:

- **confirmed** — still reproducible upstream; a filing URL is mandatory (the eight above).
- **not-applicable** — investigated, non-defect: no template references `workflow_run` / `head_sha` (U4), none uses electron-builder or signs macOS bundles (U5), action tag-pinning is a deliberate fleet-wide convention (U6).
- **obsolete** — closed since the snapshot, marked with the evidence that closed it and struck through in the recommendations list: API-docs deploy (L1), published-crate smoke test (L3), resilient buildx (L4), main-safe concurrency (L7).
- **local** — owned by `link-assistant/formal-ai` itself: cargo-lock guard (L2), link checker (L5), multi-OS matrix (L6), security scanning (L8).

**4. Documentation check.** `tests/unit/docs_requirements_issue_894.rs` parses the ledger and fails when a `confirmed` row has no `link-foundation` issue URL, when a status outside the documented vocabulary appears, when the pre-filing recommendation section returns, or when the preserved evidence goes missing.

## Scope note

The acceptance criterion says to file each confirmed gap *in the owning upstream repository*. The four still-open working-repo gaps (L2, L5, L6, L8) are owned by this repository, so they are recorded as `local` in the ledger rather than filed as new `link-assistant/formal-ai` issues. Say the word and I will open them as tracked issues too.

## Verification

```bash
cargo test --test unit docs_requirements_issue_894
# 5 passed
```

The check is falsifiable, and was falsified before being trusted: deleting the U2-rust URL from the ledger fails two of the five tests with

```
row U2-rust is confirmed but has no upstream issue URL; a confirmed finding
may never remain ready-to-file without a filing (issue #894)
```

Also run clean locally: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features`.

Requirements R894-1 … R894-4 are recorded in `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `docs/requirements-traceability.md` and `docs/case-studies/issue-894/`.

Fixes #561

## Summary
- Pass the resolved release commit SHA/version from `auto-release` and `manual-release` to the Pages deployment job.
- Make GitHub Pages checkout, artifact stamping, and the live Pages E2E wait use the same selected release SHA.
- Replace direct `cargo install rust-script` CI steps with a retrying `scripts/install-rust-script.sh` wrapper after the PR run reproduced a transient crates.io HTTP/2 install failure.
- Add workflow regression coverage plus a case-study folder with downloaded CI logs, live version evidence, screenshot, and template comparison data.

## Root Cause
The reported CI/CD run deployed Pages from the pre-release workflow SHA `0ff0455...`, where `Cargo.toml` still advertised `0.217.0`. The `auto-release` job later created the child release commit/tag for `v0.218.0`, but Pages had already stamped and uploaded the older version. The live Pages E2E check waited for the pre-release SHA too, so it passed while proving the stale deployment was live.

A follow-up PR run (`28118275692`) also exposed an unrelated CI/CD reliability problem: `Detect Changes` failed during `cargo install rust-script` because crates.io returned `[16] Error in the HTTP2 framing layer` while downloading `libc`. The neighboring version-check job installed the same tool successfully, so this PR now retries that install path.

## Reproduction

Fixes #671. Builds on the compatibility work from #647.

The previous implementation already turned the testing guide into a real
12-client matrix. This revision removes the remaining hand-maintained client
behavior, adds a human-gated learning loop over successful sessions, and makes
Formal AI execute that learning task through the real Agent CLI.

## What changed

### One registry drives every client leg

Each integration in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` now carries its
machine-readable verification contract: surface, file delivery, headless and
interactive invocation, required request/response tools, forbidden output,
launch readiness, extension, sandbox, and vendor-auth constraints.

`formal-ai clients --format json` exposes those facts and
`plan_matrix.sh` generates the GitHub Actions matrix from the registry plus the
version lock. The workflow and shell harness no longer branch on client ids.
The generated plan currently contains all 12 supported real clients:

| Surface | Clients | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI | codex, opencode, agent, gemini, claude, qwen, grok, aider | headless and real PTY tasks, streamed answer, bounded tool rounds |
| Server | t3code | launch, readiness text, HTTP response, process configuration |
| GUI | opencode-vscode, opencode-desktop | Xvfb launch, extension/process configuration |
| MCP | cursor | initialize, tools/list, real tools/call, unknown-tool refusal, vendor-auth boundary |

The existing regression cases remain: greeting/instructions separation,
interactive empty-message recovery, summarization, exact global-config undo,
real file reads, hosted-tool constraints, and recorded/replayable sessions.
The earlier matrix also found and fixed the 281-round tool loop, destructive
read-to-write routing, schema-derived absolute paths, client-working-directory
resolution, Claude's HEAD probes, and Gemini model-path logging.

### Successful sessions feed human-gated auto-learning

Every prompt-client leg now records normalized observations from two
independently worded `read_file` tasks: one headless and one interactive.

`formal-ai clients observe` normalizes a proxy JSONL transcript.
`formal-ai clients learn` groups observations by client and capability,
requires at least two distinct normalized wordings, intersects stable invoked
tools, compares observed delivery with the seeded contract, and emits a
deterministic Links Notation review artifact.

Nothing is self-applied. Every inferred amendment carries its transcript paths
and remains:

```text
decision "awaiting_human_review"
```

The committed 16-observation reference set confirms eight delivery contracts
and proposes seven stable response-tool requirements. Aider correctly produces
no tool proposal because its fixture bytes are delivered in-band.

### Formal AI performs the task through Agent CLI

The maintainer-requested reference run starts the release `formal-ai` server as
the model provider, launches Agent CLI 0.25.0, and asks Formal AI to run the
client-contract learner and write its exact stdout. The driver byte-compares
the Agent-authored file with the deterministic direct report and refuses any
result that lost the human-review gate.

The first real run exposed a general planner defect: “write its exact stdout”
was treated as literal file content. The planner now recognizes a seed-defined,
multilingual command-output frame, writes its plan, executes the explicitly
quoted command with output redirection to a safe relative target, reads the
result back, and only then completes. This is structural planner behavior, not
an issue- or command-specific rule.

The mandatory Agent CLI CI job reruns this driver on relevant changes.

## Reproduction and evidence

```bash
cargo build --release --bin formal-ai
experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/plan_matrix.sh
target/release/formal-ai clients learn \
  docs/case-studies/issue-671/agent-cli-contract-learning/observations.jsonl
experiments/agent_cli_e2e/run_issue_671_contract_learning.sh
```

- [Case study and reproduction notes](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-671-64e853f20d82/docs/case-studies/issue-671/README.md)
- [Formal AI plan executed through Agent CLI](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-671-64e853f20d82/docs/case-studies/issue-671/agent-cli-contract-learning/general-change-plan.lino)

This changes CI, CLI behavior, planner behavior, and evidence generation; it

body:
Closes #843.

## Reproduction and root cause

Before this change, a non-offline unknown prompt could turn a requested lookup
into fabricated provenance: an `example.org` URL, Unix-epoch timestamp,
prompt-derived digest, and `cache_hit` event were emitted although no transport
or cache read had happened. The same planning-versus-execution ambiguity also
affected provider, ranking, fusion, comparison, and inspection traces.

`external_search_never_fabricates_source_provenance` is the minimum regression:
it exercises the old route and proves an unexecuted lookup now records a policy
diagnostic, never source evidence.

## What changed

- Added a single capture boundary that owns the exact response bytes, URL,
  retrieval time, SHA-256, and truthful live/cache state. Live retrieval is
  opt-in; deterministic cache-only replay is the default.
- Made version-2 cache bodies content-addressed and atomically published while
  retaining version-1 compatibility. Replay validates the metadata digest
  shape before path resolution, recomputes SHA-256 from the bytes, and rejects
  corruption or attempted object-path escape.
- Routed contextual HTTP fetch and DuckDuckGo execution through that boundary.
  Provider, rank, and RRF events are emitted only after the provider response
  is captured and parsed; unavailable paths use explicit `*_planned` events.
- Added shared source-research drivers. Captured provider rankings feed RRF,
  captured pages feed `OptionNetwork::observe`, and statement probability/audit
  changes require an explicit classification of the exact capture.
- Made probability and audit provenance constructible from `SourceCapture`,
  preventing callers from assembling an unrelated URL/time/digest tuple.
  Curated registry URLs remain visible as `definition_merge:source_declared`,
  not fake HTTP retrievals.
- Added deterministic Links Notation learning proposals from captured
  observations and derived option state. Promotion to durable knowledge remains
  human-gated; live-versus-cache state is intentionally excluded so replay
  proposes the same lesson.
- Preserved offline curated-project behavior and all supported-language
  surfaces, regenerated seed closure and whole-repository self-AST artifacts,
  and added a patch changelog fragment.
- Hardened desktop CI discovered during fresh branch runs: Windows desktop
  builds bypass `sccache` to preserve Cargo response-file handling, while macOS
  DMG creation retries only the documented transient `hdiutil` errors with a
  bounded three-attempt policy.

The implementation and acceptance map are documented in
[`docs/case-studies/issue-843/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-843-3a81d665c7bc/docs/case-studies/issue-843).

## Automated verification

The focused issue suite contains 11 regressions, including:

- exact-byte live capture and byte-identical offline replay;
- real provider rankings reaching RRF;
- capture-backed option learning and deterministic proposals;
- capture-bound statement classification and audit conversion;
- no evidence on cache miss or transport failure;
- metadata digest/path traversal rejection;
- one composed provider → RRF → option → statement → audit → replay task;
- preservation of the same-task Agent CLI authorship evidence.

Final local gates on commit `e78f4a7df04dc1669d14db5173d97ffa20be2612`
after merging `origin/main`:

- `cargo test --lib --bins --tests --all-features --verbose`
  - library: 241 passed;
  - source suite: 482 passed;
  - main unit aggregate: 2,176 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored;
  - every binary and integration aggregate: 0 failed.
- `cargo test --doc --verbose`
- `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check --examples --all-features`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, locked Cargo metadata, and PR-wide
  `git diff --check`
- default and docs.rs-profile rustdoc with warnings denied
- actionlint 1.7.7 and ShellCheck 0.10.0 over the exact CI selector
- self-AST/census byte equality, seed closure, changelog reconstruction,
  release-script, file-size, terminology, hardcoded-language, disk-policy, and
  worker-line-budget gates
- `sh src/web/wasm-worker/build.sh` and the worker size budget
  (107,248 bytes of 524,288)

No test uses the live network. Fixture transports enter through the production
capture client and replay through the production cache path.

## Same-task Formal AI self-application

External Agent CLI session `ses_052d57d6affe1f2GYFodXhrqPl`, served by the
`formal-ai` model, completed a smallest leaf of this exact task in four rounds:
it planned, wrote, read back, and completed the canonical
`source-evidence-honesty-invariant.lino`. The generated artifact is byte-for-byte
equal to `data/meta/source-evidence-honesty-invariant.lino`.

The reviewed five-leaf decomposition records one Agent-CLI-authored leaf (20%).
Raw client/server traces and the replay harness are committed under
[`self-hosting-authorship/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-843-3a81d665c7bc/docs/case-studies/issue-843/self-hosting-authorship)
and [`experiments/issue_843_self_authoring/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-843-3a81d665c7bc/experiments/issue_843_self_authoring).

After merging the latest self-hosting changes from `main`, release Formal AI
session `ses_05213155bffe5aZC48rv0KnwPr` regenerated the canonical self-AST.
Its committed output is byte-for-byte equal to `data/meta/self-ast.lino`, and
the refreshed issue-842 workspace census is byte-for-byte equal to the canonical
334-document census. Evidence is under
[`post-merge-self-ast/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-843-3a81d665c7bc/docs/case-studies/issue-843/post-merge-self-ast).

The earlier whole-repository source-links projection remains complementary
self-model evidence and is not counted as same-task authorship.

This is a non-visual execution/provenance change, so no before/after UI
screenshots apply.

## CI follow-up

Fresh desktop CI exposed a Windows-only `sccache 0.17.0` limitation while
compiling `web-sys 0.3.103`: the wrapper respawned `rustc` with the expanded
feature-check command and failed with CreateProcess error 206 on both x64 and
ARM64. Desktop builds now bypass sccache only on Windows, allowing Cargo to use
its response-file path; Unix compiler-output caching remains enabled. A
release-workflow regression pins both platform conditions.

Fresh macOS ARM64 jobs then reproduced the GitHub-hosted runner disk-image
failure `hdiutil: create failed - Device not configured` twice, after signing
and ZIP creation had succeeded. Following the runner-image maintainers’
documented mitigation in
[actions/runner-images#7522](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/7522),
both macOS package paths now use a bounded wrapper: it retries only
`Device not configured`, `Resource busy`, or `No child processes`; removes only
an incomplete top-level DMG; calls `sync`; and backs off for at most three
attempts. Signing, notarization, dependency, and all other builder errors still
fail immediately. Three behavioral regressions verify recovery/cleanup,
unrelated-error fail-fast behavior, and the attempt ceiling.

body:
Fixes #991

## What this changes

Issue #991 is the remainder of #710 row 20: after #444/PR #448 delivered the
discovery plan and #709/PR #884 delivered the source-tier and contradiction
policy, a procedural request still returned a description of the work the solver
*would* do rather than the guide itself.

`how to make pancakes?` before this pull request
(`docs/case-studies/issue-991/raw-data/before-fix-run.txt`, captured from a
binary built at this branch's base commit):

```text
Procedural discovery plan for `make pancakes` (action `make`, object `pancakes`).
I do not answer this from a memoized recipe. The solver first checks Wikipedia …
```

and after (`raw-data/after-fix-run.txt`, a real `formal-ai serve` process over
`/api/openai/v1/chat/completions`):

```text
## How to make pancakes

1. 2 cups (18oz/510g) self-rising or all-purpose flour (See tips below) — wikiHow (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, sha256 1cbdf5f7a9d6)
2. 2 tablespoons of butter or vegetable oil — wikiHow (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, sha256 1cbdf5f7a9d6)
…
### Sources
- wikihow — contributed (1 page(s), 12 step(s))
- stackexchange — contributed (2 page(s), 6 step(s))
…
Bounds: max_depth=2 max_pages_per_service=4 max_services=4 max_steps=12
```

Review on this pull request then asked for two more things, and both are here:
the probability of merge conflicts in the files this branch touched is reduced
to zero for every structural cause, measured rather than asserted; and the
issue's vision is advanced with failure-driven task decomposition executed
through real Agent CLIs.

## How it works

- **One bounded contract, two runtimes.** `src/how_to_guide.rs` (with
  `extract.rs`, `render.rs`) selects services from
  `data/seed/sources-registry.lino` — never a hardcoded list — and orders
  accepted steps by the #709 source tier, then depth, source, and position.
  `src/web/worker/formal_ai_worker_24.js` mirrors it for the browser. Both are
  checked against one recorded expectation
  (`tests/fixtures/issue-991/expected-guides.json`, written from the Rust path by
  `examples/issue_991_how_to_parity.rs`), so they cannot drift apart silently.
- **Recursion to the page that holds the procedure.** A relevant Stack Exchange
  question at depth 0 is followed to its answers at depth 1; a listless wiki page
  to its same-wiki links — inside `max_depth=2 max_pages_per_service=4
  max_services=4 max_steps=12` and a capture-age bound.
- **Provenance on every step**: source id, exact URL, license, sha256 digest, and
  depth.
- **Opt-outs stay authoritative**: a service whose `settings_key` is disabled is
  reported as `disabled` with zero pages and zero steps and is never contacted.
- **Seven-day accessibility memory**: `src/service_accessibility.rs` records
  success *and* failure per service with a `7 * 24 * 60 * 60` second TTL in the
  environment's associative memory, with explicit `needs_refresh`, `invalidate`,
  and `invalidate_all`. A failure on a fallback endpoint is recorded as
  `fallback_failed` so it does not condemn a service whose entry endpoint works.
- **No prose in the engine (R379).** Every reader-facing fragment of the guide —
  headings, the step template, the citation and conflict lines, the insufficient
  evidence sentence — lives in `data/seed/multilingual-responses-procedure.lino`
  under a `how_to_guide_*` intent seeded in en/ru/hi/zh. `render.rs` reads it via
  `seed::localized_response` and the worker via `answerFor`, so
  `HowToGuide::markdown_in("ru")` renders the same evidence in another language
  instead of translating it afterwards. Machine-readable output (trace lines,
  evidence events, the accessibility projection, capture-drift details) goes
  through the new `src/trace_record.rs`: an event slug plus `key=value` fields.
- **Insufficient evidence is reported, not filled in**: a run below the minimum
  accepted steps asserts no procedure.

## Merge conflicts, measured and removed

> "We need to find a way to reduce possibility of conflicts in these files in the
> future. […] The end result should be that probability of conflicts in the
> future reduced to zero." — review on this pull request

Nothing here is an estimate. `python3 scripts/analyze-merge-conflicts.py`
replays every merge commit in this repository with `git merge-tree` and counts
the paths git could not merge by itself: **884 merges, 1914 conflict events, 423
distinct paths**. The full write-up is
[`docs/case-studies/issue-991/merge-conflict-analysis.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-991-43e4ba3ff505/docs/case-studies/issue-991/merge-conflict-analysis.md);
the raw run and the ranked ledger are committed beside it.

| Structural cause | Events | Share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| shared-source | 715 | 37.4% |
| derived-artifact | 481 | 25.1% |
| append-only-list | 411 | 21.5% |
| append-only-document | 126 | 6.6% |
| lockfile-or-manifest | 60 | 3.1% |
| automation-placeholder | 44 | 2.3% |
| ci-workflow | 36 | 1.9% |
| other | 30 | 1.6% |
| sequential-file-name | 11 | 0.6% |

The distribution is the finding: only the top row is people disagreeing about
behaviour. The other 62.6% is *layout* — files that conflict because of where
their content sits. Three of those causes had no mechanism before, and each one
now gets the same treatment: **extract the append point, union the extract,
verify the union.**

- **CI workflow (36 events).** `.github/workflows/release.yml` was the third most
  conflicted path because its lint job was one appended step per check. A check
  is now one file under `data/meta/ci-gates/` named after the check (36 shards),
  and the workflow runs `rust-script scripts/run-ci-gates.rs --stage <stage>`
  once per stage without ever naming an individual gate. Two branches adding
  gates write two differently named files, so there is nothing left to conflict
  on — and nothing to union either.
- **The seed inventory (41).** `src/seed/embedded.rs` and `src/web/seed_loader.js`
  each carried their own copy of the `data/seed/*.lino` list, so adding a seed
  file meant appending to the same lines in two files — and the copies could
  disagree about which files exist. Both now generate from one union-merged
  registry, `data/meta/seed-registry.lino`. This is a correctness fix as much as
  a conflict fix: the Rust engine and the browser worker can no longer disagree
  about the corpus.
- **Global scalar ratchet.** One constant recording a repository-wide total makes
  every branch rewrite the same line; the worker line budget is now one shard per
  module, summed.

What keeps this from unwinding is that the policy is itself checked. Four gates:

| Gate | Fails when |
| --- | --- |
| `check-merge-conflict-policy` | a ranked ledger path is neither mechanized nor deferred, a registry path is not actually `merge=union` in git, a `merge=union` line is missing from the registry, or a union artifact has no verifier |
| `check-ordered-lists-are-canonical` | a union-merged list is out of order or holds a repeat |
| `check-seed-registry` | the Rust or browser seed inventory drifted from `data/meta/seed-registry.lino` |
| `check-ci-gate-registry` | the lint job runs a gate command inline instead of through the registry |

The union-merge invariant is explicit and enforced: *every union-merged path has
a verifier that fails while the unioned result is not canonical*, unless it
declares `union_is_terminal` because every possible union of it is already
correct. `bash scripts/regenerate-derived-artifacts.sh` turns a post-merge union
back into the one correct file, and `--check` fails when anything is stale.

**First live merge through the mechanism** (`247be10c`, merging `main` at
`5e20deda` / PR #1005). Git stopped on exactly one path, `src/seed/embedded.rs`,
and only because PR #1005 was written before the registry existed: it appended
`learned-methods.lino` to the three hand-ordered lists this branch had already
replaced with `include!("embedded_registry.rs")`. Resolving it meant adding one
`seed learned-methods` block to `data/meta/seed-registry.lino` and running
`rust-script scripts/generate-seed-registry.rs --write` — no hand-editing of
either projection. Every other path this branch and PR #1005 both touched
(`src/lib.rs`, `tests/unit/mod.rs`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`, the
self-AST census, `REQUIREMENTS.md`) merged without stopping, and
`bash scripts/regenerate-derived-artifacts.sh` restored all of them; `--check`
then reported every derived artifact current. `REQUIREMENTS.md` is the case that
shows why the verifier matters rather than the union alone: the union had spliced
PR #1005's issue #922 section into #919's body under #891's heading, a silently
wrong file that no conflict marker would have flagged. The section moved to
`docs/requirements/issue-0922-method-learning-from-experience.md` and the
assembled document now carries every heading `main` has.

Five deferrals are recorded with reasons, and the honest one is first:
`shared_logic_edits`. Two branches changing the same behaviour in the same
function is a real semantic collision; no file layout decides it for them, and
mechanizing it would be lying. So *reduced to zero* is claimed for the
structural causes and explicitly not claimed for the semantic one — which is the
point of measuring rather than asserting.

Contributing guidelines gained the rule in the same terms
(`CONTRIBUTING.md`): a list that grows by appending belongs in its own file.

## Splitting a failing task from its own failure

> "…incremental decomposition, so if big task is failing, we try to split them
> and solve them using Formal AI and Agent CLI locally, and continue splitting
> until tasks are fully solvable" — review on this pull request

`--decompose` already existed, but it plans *before* it has evidence: it splits
whether or not the CLI needed the split. This adds the inverse protocol.

- `TaskExecutor` gained a `split` hook — defaulted, so every existing executor is
  unchanged — and `solve_recursively` now shrinks a failed task from the evidence
  that attempt produced. `solve_recursively_within` lets a caller choose the
  bound; zero reproduces the previous plan-driven protocol exactly.
- `SplittingExecutor` answers that hook with **the repository's own**
  `decompose_task_with_ledger`, one level per split, refuses a child that repeats
  its parent, and records each split with the failure that justified it. Formal
  AI is decomposing its own work with its own decomposer.
- `formal-ai agent dispatch --incremental` runs the protocol against real agent
  CLIs: the whole task is attempted first, a passing attempt's effects reach the
  workspace *before* the next attempt starts (so pieces build on each other and
  the retried parent sees their work), an irreducible failure escalates to the
  next `--cli`, and an exhausted list is reported blocked rather than silently
  retried. Exit status reflects the root task only.
- **Every blocked task becomes a review request**, mirrored to `proposals.lino`
  next to the report: the task, each CLI that tried it, the evidence each attempt
  produced, and `status "human_review_required"`. A run cannot approve its own
  extension, so this is the same gate a learned decomposition strategy passes
  through. A run that solved everything still writes the document, empty but for
  its header — "nothing to propose" and "the run never got that far" are
  different answers.

The integration test drives this through the real process boundary: an external
script CLI that fails a task above a size limit, splits, solves the pieces, and
then solves the parent it originally refused.

## Reproducing and testing

Committed real-service captures live in `tests/fixtures/issue-991/` with their
timestamps, sha256 digests, byte counts, and licenses in
`capture-manifest.lino`. The suite replays them with the transport disabled, so
it is deterministic and offline; `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_FETCH=1` re-fetches through the
same production path and reports drift.

| Surface | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Native | `tests/unit/issue_991_how_to_synthesis.rs` (9 tests) |
| HTTP agent/API | `tests/integration/issue_991_how_to_http.rs` (3 tests, real server process) |
| Browser | `tests/web/issue-991-how-to-synthesis.test.mjs` |
| Conflict-free layout | `tests/unit/ci_gates.rs`, `check-merge-conflict-policy`, `check-seed-registry`, `check-ci-gate-registry` |
| Incremental decomposition | `tests/unit/issue_991_incremental_decomposition.rs` (in process) |
| Incremental dispatch | `tests/integration/issue_991_incremental_dispatch.rs` (4 tests, real agent CLI processes) |

All of them fail against the base commit and pass here, through the real
production paths rather than stubs.

Local checks: `rust-script scripts/run-ci-gates.rs --stage rust|wasm|web` clean
(the whole registry, which includes `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests
--all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --examples --all-features`, and
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`); `cargo test --test unit` 2704 passed / 3 ignored,
`cargo test --test integration` 340 passed / 1 ignored, `cargo test --doc`
clean, `npm run test:web` 63/63.

## Documentation

- `docs/case-studies/issue-991/README.md` — symptom, root causes, the fix,
  before/after captures, the raw GitHub data, and the known lexical-relevance
  limitation.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-991/merge-conflict-analysis.md` — the conflict
  measurement, the five shapes, the union invariant, and the honest deferrals.
- `docs/configuration/orchestration.md` — `--incremental`, with the
  `proposals.lino` shape.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` — `## Issue #991`, rows R991-1…R991-9 (R991-8 the structural
  zero-conflict guarantee, R991-9 failure-driven splitting), assembled from
  `docs/requirements/`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — the append-only-list rule and the post-merge
  regeneration step.

## Incidental

- `tests/integration/http_server.rs` gained `spawn_formal_ai_server_with_env`, so
  a test can configure the server child rather than the shared test process.
- Merging `main` regenerated the self-AST census documents
  (`cargo run --example regenerate_self_ast_census`) and took `main`'s resolution
  of `tests/issue_961_macos_portability.rs`.
- `scripts/check-disk-usage-policy.rs` now reads the gate registry as well as
  `release.yml`, because the commands CI runs are no longer all in the workflow
  text.

Fixes #864.

## Summary

- proactively append a seed-backed, localized issue-report consent invitation after unresolved reasoning and detected tool failures
- classify browser/desktop failures from solver intents and structured provider/tool signals, persist the failure bit, and aggregate it across Agent-plan steps
- reuse #839's six-section contextual report action without automatically filing anything
- preserve reproducible red/green browser screenshots, live `@link-assistant/agent` evidence, requirement traceability, and a dedicated Agent CLI CI replay

## Root cause and reproduction

Issue #839 made `Report issue` user-initiated and contextual, but no failure path actively offered it. Unknown reasoning stopped after its diagnostic, structured tool failures only rendered an error, Agent CLI plain-text shell failures could be presented as successful output, and the UI only exposed the old passive action for `intent: unknown`.

The retained red regressions reproduce both boundaries:

```sh
cargo test --test unit issue_864 -- --nocapture
cd tests/e2e && npx playwright test --config=playwright.local.config.js tests/issue-864.spec.js
```

Their pre-fix output is under `docs/case-studies/issue-864/raw-data/`. The live replay runs an exact nonexistent command because Agent CLI serializes silent `false` output without an observable exit code:

```sh
cargo build --release --bin formal-ai
experiments/agent_cli_e2e/run_issue_864.sh
```

## Behavioral boundary

- failures: unknown reasoning, explicit failure intents, `ok: false`, `success: false`, non-zero exit status, HTTP errors, explicit error fields, and seeded plain-text shell failure signals
- expected stops: refusal, denial, cancellation, abort, pending approval, and missing grants
- ordinary assistant prose containing words such as “error” or “failed” is not classified as a failure
- detection only offers consent; it never invokes `gh` or files an issue

## Browser evidence

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Failure without proactive invitation](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-864-c5dca48884f5/docs/case-studies/issue-864/before.png?raw=true) | ![Failure with proactive invitation](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-864-c5dca48884f5/docs/case-studies/issue-864/after.png?raw=true) |

## Verification
- GitHub Actions on final SHA: 38 passed, 8 expected skips, 0 failed

- Rust unit suite: 2,397 passed, 3 ignored
- Rust integration suite (serial): 299 passed, 1 ignored
- standalone Rust test targets: 95 passed; doctests passed
- post-merge issue #864 contract: 11 passed; unknown-reasoning invariant: 1 passed; self-AST fidelity: 7 passed
- focused Playwright regression: 2 passed on the merged tree
- full Playwright suite executed in two shards; one unrelated issue-845 worker-startup timing failure passed on immediate isolated replay, without increasing timeouts
- real Agent CLI ↔ live Formal AI replay: 2 completion rounds, failed command preserved, opt-in invitation present, no automatic filing
- `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check --examples --all-features`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --lib`
- closure, seed-sync, file-size, hardcoded-language, i18n, locale parity, intent coverage, web TDZ, UI-string, formatting, workflow, syntax, and whitespace guards

The full investigation, requirements matrix, screenshots, red logs, and raw green evidence are in `docs/case-studies/issue-864/`.

## Replace the stale Spider-Man release-order seed with current source-backed data

Fixes #892.

### Root cause

`data/seed/facts.lino` answered "list the Spider-Man films in release order" from a
frozen sentence (`summary`) typed by hand. A sentence cannot gain a newly released
film, cannot keep a list ordered, and cannot tell an announced title from a released
one — so the record went stale the moment the next film came out, exactly as the
audit (verdict `still-broken`) reported.

### Solution

The answer is now *computed* at question time from a checked-in, timestamped,
source-backed snapshot. Nothing about the mechanism is Spider-Man specific.

1. **Source-backed structured data.** `data/cache/wikidata/query/spider-man-title-role-films.rq`
   is a SPARQL query against the Wikidata Query Service that selects the feature films
   in which Spider-Man plays the title role, deriving series membership from
   `Q2307877 wdt:P527` and excluding TV films, shorts and fan films *structurally*
   rather than by a hardcoded list. Its raw answer is checked in as `.json` (plus the
   canonical `.lino` twin), together with the entity cache of every returned film.
2. **Ordering and announced titles.** `data/seed/release-timelines.lino` is a general
   release-timeline registry: per-language answer wording, and per timeline its
   subject, source, query file, cache file, snapshot date, freshness window, SHA-256,
   and every work with its release date and localized titles.
   `formal_ai::release_timeline` renders it for a language as of a given day: released
   works ordered by date and numbered, works dated in the future (or with no announced
   date) listed separately as announced.
3. **Deterministic offline behaviour + provenance.** The snapshot is committed, so the
   answer is identical offline and in CI. `scripts/ground-release-timelines.py`
   regenerates the seed from the cache (`--check` verifies byte equality, `--refresh`
   re-fetches), and the recorded SHA-256 is asserted against the snapshot bytes by a
   test. Once the snapshot outlives its freshness window the answer keeps working but
   switches to stale wording that names the snapshot date and warns that later
   releases may be missing. `release_timeline:*` evidence links record which snapshot
   an answer came from, its digest, the released/announced counts and staleness.

### Example output (today = 2026-08-04)

> Released title-role Spider-Man films in release order: 1. Spider-Man (2002); … 10.
> Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (2023); 11. Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026).
> Announced but not yet released: Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse (2027-06-18).
> Source: Wikidata Query Service, snapshot taken 2026-08-04.

### Tests

`tests/unit/specification/issue_892.rs` — one test per acceptance criterion plus a
whole-task test, all against fixed days so they never depend on when the suite runs:

- `current_snapshot_lists_released_works_in_date_order` — released works in date order,
  exact rendered text.
- `stale_snapshot_still_answers_but_flags_the_gap` — day 180 fresh vs day 181 stale;
  staleness changes wording, never classification.
- `a_future_release_is_announced_until_its_release_day` — announced the day before,
  released on the day.
- `an_undated_work_is_never_reported_as_released`.
- `the_seeded_spider_man_timeline_is_grounded_and_ordered`.
- `the_seeded_timeline_is_a_transcription_of_the_checked_in_cache` — every date
  re-read from the SPARQL answer, every title from the entity cache, digest recomputed.
- `spider_man_answers_come_from_the_snapshot_not_from_a_sentence` — end-to-end through
  the solver, including the evidence links and the reasoning step.
- `every_registered_language_gets_its_own_release_timeline_wording` — reads the language
  registry (`formal_ai::language::registered_languages()`) and asserts that every
  registered language, Spanish included, has its own phrasing, subject and per-film
  titles, and that no two languages share a heading (i.e. nothing silently falls back
  to English).

The seed and `scripts/ground-release-timelines.py` are driven by
`data/seed/languages.lino`, so registering a new language is what makes the script ask
the source for that language's labels — the list is not hardcoded. The Wikidata entity
caches were re-fetched so they carry the Spanish labels.

`tests/unit/specification/issue_462.rs` is now language-aware: it asserts release order
against the rendered timeline for each language instead of a frozen English list.

### Verification

- `cargo test --test unit` — 2537 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test --test integration` — 306 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `python3 scripts/ground-release-timelines.py --check` — seed matches the cache.
- `python3 scripts/audit-total-closure.py --json .` — 0 unresolved tokens.
- `node tests/e2e/scripts/check-language-test-coverage.mjs` — OK for en, ru, hi, zh, es.
title: Replace the stale Spider-Man release-order seed with current source-backed data

Fixes #896.

## Summary

- route native DuckDuckGo research through `web-capture`'s published URL/parser API and `web-search`'s published merger while retaining Formal AI's exact-byte cached transport
- bundle `@link-assistant/web-search` into the production browser worker and prefer web-capture's `GET /fetch?url=...` contract for explicit URL capture
- retain provenance, cache-only replay, target status/body, cancellation deadlines, and component diagnostics across both boundaries
- keep the old Instant Answer, WASM/local merger, and direct-CORS paths as bounded, explicitly diagnosed compatibility fallbacks
- add locked production dependencies, deterministic bundle checks, a changelog fragment, integration evidence, and the issue #896 case study

## Reproduction and verification

Before this change, neither published component was a production dependency: native research called DuckDuckGo's Instant Answer API directly, browser search used Formal AI's merger, and browser fetch called target URLs directly.

The native regression fixture accepts only the URL produced by `web_capture::search`, then verifies parsed rankings cross `web_search::merger`, exact captured bytes replay offline without another transport call, and both component/fallback failures remain visible. The real-worker Playwright fixture verifies the published registry and merger in English, Russian, Hindi, Chinese, and Spanish; it also proves web-capture preserves a target 503 and exact body, diagnoses network failure, and aborts a timed-out component request before bounded fallback.

Local checks:

- `cargo test --test unit` — 2473 passed, 3 ignored (after merging `main`)
- `cargo test --test integration --all-features` — 299 passed, 1 ignored
- `cargo test --test source --all-features` — 482 passed
- standalone tests, examples, Clippy with `-D warnings`, rustdoc/docs.rs builds, formatting, WASM/size, changelog, dependency-lock, and repository policy gates — passed
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run build:web` — passed with no generated diff
- `bunx playwright test --config playwright.local.config.js tests/issue-896.spec.js` — 8 passed
- cold `docker build` — full 17.4 GB image export passed, and an explicit container invocation reported `formal-ai 0.323.0`
- complete local browser coverage — 386 tests passed before this host reached the unchanged 15-minute aggregate cap; the entire remaining 110-test multilingual group then passed separately, covering all 464 collected tests. Recent `main` CI runs the same suite successfully within the job cap.

This changes no rendered UI, so before/after screenshots are not applicable.

## Upstream gaps and bounded workarounds

- https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/issues/21 tracks caller-owned transport, cancellation, per-provider errors, and exact receipts
- https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/147 tracks injectable transport, cancellation, and exact response receipts
- https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/issues/22 tracks a merge-only feature independent of server and capture dependencies
- https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/148 tracks a pure-adapter feature independent of browser and server dependencies

The unconditional runtime graphs currently pull native TLS into merge/adapter-only Rust consumers. The bounded Docker workaround installs `pkg-config` and `libssl-dev` in the builder only; the runtime image is unchanged. A cold macOS x64 release compile took 33m21s and was cancelled during DMG creation at the former 40-minute cap in [Desktop run 30788311906](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/30788311906), so that target now receives a bounded 50-minute budget. Both Windows targets moved the same way in [Desktop run 30832897812](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/30832897812) — windows-x64 compiled for 17m39s, packaged a valid installer, and was cancelled at the cap while uploading its checksum fragment, with windows-arm64 finishing at 36m04s — so they share the same 50-minute budget; the Linux and macOS ARM64 targets stay well under 40 minutes and keep it. The same graph also moved the Linux `Build Package` job from roughly 4-5 minutes on `main` to 7m14s here, and a cold `cargo build --release` after a `Cargo.lock` change exceeded its former 10-minute cap in [run 30828819505](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/30828819505), so that job now has a bounded 15-minute budget. Adapter, build-package, timeout-exception, and fallback removal conditions are documented in `docs/case-studies/issue-896/README.md`.

## Self-hosting evidence

Formal AI served the external Agent CLI session that authored one of five reviewed smallest leaves (20%). The generated invariant is compared byte-for-byte with the canonical artifact. Session, raw traces, decomposition, and replay harness are retained under `docs/case-studies/issue-896/self-hosting-authorship/` and `experiments/issue_896_self_authoring/`.

body:
Fixes #973.

## The problem

The automated `solve` run on PR #927 (linked issue #905) failed on 2026-08-04 at
04:05:17Z and left exactly one artefact — [this comment](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/927#issuecomment-5174474849):

> **Reason**
> ```text
> AGENT execution failed with Agent reported error: [object Object]
> ```
> Logs were not attached because `--attach-logs` was not enabled.

The renderer half is fixed upstream (link-assistant/hive-mind#2141 →
link-assistant/hive-mind#2143; reported against the Agent CLI as
link-assistant/agent#289 and link-assistant/agent#290). This PR fixes the half
this repository owns: **the run configuration**. The run was started without
`--attach-logs`, so when the rendered reason turned out to be useless there was
no second source. The container is gone and that cause is unrecoverable.

A failure whose recorded reason is `[object Object]` is unlearnable by
construction — the next iteration of the self/auto-learning loop has nothing to
act on.

## How to reproduce

```bash
# before this PR — the configuration that produced the unrecoverable failure
grep 'exec solve' examples/self-coding/run.sh
#   exec solve "$2" --tool agent --model formal-ai --verbose      <- no --attach-logs
```

## What changed

- **`examples/self-coding/run.sh`** — the `--live` entry point now runs
  `solve "$2" --tool agent --model formal-ai --attach-logs --verbose`.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — a new section, *Always run automated `solve` sessions
  with `--attach-logs --verbose`*, with the canonical command and why neither
  flag substitutes for the other: `--attach-logs` publishes the session log to
  the pull request; `--verbose` is what makes the Agent adapter dump the **raw
  JSON** of every error and fatal-startup record (hive-mind#2143) — the record
  that survives a payload shape the renderer does not know.
- **`tests/issue_973_solve_flags.rs`** — the policy is enforced, not just
  written down. The scan reads the guides and scripts this repository publishes
  (`docs/`, `examples/`, `scripts/`, `.github/`, `src/`, root guides), joins
  shell/Markdown line continuations so a wrapped command is judged whole,
  ignores prose such as "we do not solve a task by hand", and fails naming the
  file, line and missing flag. Recorded history under `docs/case-studies/`,
  `dev/log/` and `experiments/` is exempt — a past run stays as it happened
  (same exemption list `scripts/detect-code-changes.rs` already uses).
- **`docs/case-studies/issue-973/`** — timeline, root causes RC1–RC6, prior art,
  and the captured GitHub API evidence under `raw-data/` (the failure comment,
  the full PR #927 comment manifest showing the contrast with a later run that
  *did* attach a log).
- **`REQUIREMENTS.md` / `docs/requirements-traceability.md`** — R973-1..R973-3
  with the delivering PR, the pinning test, and the falsification runs.
- **`changelog.d/20260805_110000_issue_973_solve_evidence_flags.md`** — patch bump.

## Verification

```
$ cargo test --test issue_973_solve_flags
running 4 tests
test contributing_explains_why_both_flags_are_load_bearing ... ok
test the_case_study_records_the_unrecoverable_failure_and_the_fix ... ok
test the_live_self_coding_entry_point_attaches_logs_and_runs_verbose ... ok
test every_published_solve_invocation_carries_both_evidence_flags ... ok

test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed
```

Falsified both guards (red before green), not just observed green:

- removing `--attach-logs` from `examples/self-coding/run.sh` →
  `examples/self-coding/run.sh:14 publishes a solve invocation without --attach-logs; a run started without both flags can fail with no recoverable evidence (issue #973)`
- removing `--verbose` from the CONTRIBUTING command →
  `CONTRIBUTING.md:115 publishes a solve invocation without --verbose; ...`

`cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features` are clean.
title: Require --attach-logs --verbose on every published solve invocation

body:
Fixes #812.

The issue asks for every false positive, false negative, warning and error in CI/CD. The second class — checks that pass without checking — turned out to be the larger one, and it is what was actually blocking releases. Every finding below was reproduced locally before it was fixed; the evidence, timeline and per-finding disposition live in [`dev/log/issues/812/pulls/813/`](dev/log/issues/812/pulls/813/analysis.md).

## The two failures that were actually red

**1. `Auto Release` deadlocked on the self-hosting ratchet.** Two independent root causes:

- *The denominator measured log volume, not authorship.* 599,340 of the 636,240 lines in `v0.300.0..main` — **94.20%** — were captured CI transcripts and lockfiles that this repository *requires* each iteration to commit. Committing the evidence the process demands was itself scored as a regression, so the ratchet could only ever tighten past reach. Artifacts (`*.log`, `*.jsonl`, `*.diff`, `*.patch`, `*.stderr`, `*.stdout`) and lockfiles are now excluded symmetrically from both sides of the ratio, under a new `METRIC_VERSION = 2` so the change starts a fresh comparison epoch instead of silently invalidating recorded history.
- *Enforcement sat where nobody could act on it.* It ran in `record_release`, on `main`, after every contributing commit was already immutable — and it blocked the only mechanism that advances the range. Release-time is now `RatchetPolicy::Report`; enforcement moved to a differential (branch-vs-base) pull-request gate, where the commits can still be amended.

Verified: the exact command that failed in CI now exits 0 — `4.36% (1608/36896 changed lines; 10/119 commits)`.

**2. macOS desktop codesigning.** Not a packaging defect. Run 29752745259 is a `workflow_run` *healing* build of tag `v0.300.0`, which predates the four packaging fixes already merged; the fixed code is proven green in PR run 29746221627 (`considered=1479 skipped=751`). It needs a newer tag, which fix 1 unblocks. Rather than leave this to be re-diagnosed every time, `scripts/desktop-release-resolve.sh` now emits a `::notice` when it is packaging a tag that is not the tip of the default branch.

## Checks that never gated

| What | Why it was green |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo clippy` | Ran without `-D warnings`. Every lint in `[lints.clippy]` is `warn`, so the job printed findings and exited 0. The tree is clean today, so adding it promotes existing behaviour rather than introducing failures. |
| `scripts/check-file-size.rs` | Matched directory exclusions as **substrings**, so `.git` hid all of `.github/workflows/**`. Exclusions are now matched per path component; workflows are measured (warn 1500, fail 2000), while third-party workflows quoted under `docs/case-studies/**` stay exempt — reformatting them would destroy the thing they document. |
| workflow definitions and shell scripts | Nothing validated either. A mistyped `needs.<job>` reference fails **open**: the guarded step silently skips under a green check. `actionlint` 1.7.7 (shellcheck-embedded) and `shellcheck --severity=warning` now run in `lint`. |
| desktop library tests | `node --test $(ls … \| grep -v …)` fell back to Node's own discovery whenever the glob stopped matching — a green step running none of the intended tests. The list is built explicitly and an empty list is a hard error. |

## Checks that gated the wrong thing

- `auto-release`/`manual-release` needed only `[lint, test, build]`. A red **`Secrets Scan`** or either E2E suite on `main` still published the crate, the Docker image and the GitHub Release. (`docker-build` is deliberately *not* a gate: it publishes independently and its failure must not block the crate.)
- The desktop `finalize` job ran under `always()`, so a **cancelled** run could `gh release upload --clobber` a partial `SHA256SUMS.txt` over a complete one. Now `!cancelled()`.
- Desktop packaging and VS Code jobs validated a stale merge preview; they now simulate the fresh merge, as `lint`/`test` already did.
- `secretlint` floated to whatever `latest` was at run time. Pinned.
- `$BASE_REF` was unquoted in `scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` — a word-split there takes the *skip* branch and reports success without merging.
- `upload-pages-artifact` dropped dotfiles (`include-hidden-files: true`); the screenshot upload was `if: always()` with the default `if-no-files-found: warn`, i.e. green on an empty artifact.

One finding was deliberately **not** "fixed": `scripts/install.sh` is the only script without `pipefail`, because it is the only one running under `#!/usr/bin/env sh`. `pipefail` is not POSIX and aborts dash — the `/bin/sh` a `curl … | sh` install lands in. The rationale is now recorded in the file header so it is not "fixed" later.

## Upstream reports

Three defects reproduce in the templates themselves; all were re-verified against upstream `main` via the API before reporting.

- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#111 — **filed in this iteration**: unquoted `$BASE_REF` in `simulate-fresh-merge.sh`, with a reproduction, a workaround and a suggested fix. (The rust template's copy quotes correctly; python does not ship the script.)
- link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#33 and #35 — already open upstream, so recorded rather than re-filed.

## Verification

- `cargo test --test unit` → **1953 passed, 0 failed** (6 new regression tests)
- `actionlint -shellcheck` over every workflow → exit 0 (type-checking confirmed live by injecting a bogus `needs.secrets-scanX` into a copy and observing the error)
- `shellcheck --severity=warning` over the 17 shipped scripts → exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs` → exit 0

New tests: `releases_do_not_publish_past_a_failing_secrets_scan_or_e2e_suite`, `lint_job_gates_on_workflow_shell_and_clippy_findings`, `check_directory_measures_github_workflows`, `check_directory_does_not_measure_quoted_case_study_workflows`, plus the ratchet exclusion and differential-gate tests.

## Debug output (default off, per the issue)

- `FORMAL_AI_MACOS_SIGN_DEBUG=1` — per-path `[adhoc-sign-mac]` sign decisions; its *absence* from the failing log is what proved the healing-build diagnosis.
- `experiments/self_hosting_ratchet_replay/replay.py` — per-commit attribution, reason and subject for any range, without `rust-script`.

## Second pass: defects found by running the fixed pipeline

Run [29767811026](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29767811026) was the first full run of the repaired pipeline, and it found two more — one introduced by this PR's own first commit.

**`Test (ubuntu-latest)` reported failure with 1953 tests passed and 0 failed.** The suite finished at 18:43:50; `timeout-minutes: 15` killed the job 1.1 seconds later, during teardown. Run 29749095334 on `main` had already done exactly this and was never diagnosed, because GitHub renders a timeout as `cancelled` — indistinguishable from an infrastructure blip. The budget was not padding: checkout plus the two data checks cost ~3m15s before a test runs, the suite takes ~11m, and eight individual agentic/driver tests each exceed 60 s. Recent `main` durations show creep rather than a one-off — 11m02s, 12m27s, 11m49s, 12m57s, **15m16s (cancelled)**, 14m13s. The budget now matches measured cost, and the step emits a `::warning` past 70% of it so the margin cannot be eaten again in silence. Making those eight tests cheaper is separate work with its own regression risk; what is fixed here is the false report.

**The release gates I added would have accepted a timed-out job.** They read `needs.<job>.result != 'failure'`, chosen so a legitimately *skipped* job would not block a release — but the finding above is the proof that a timeout resolves to `'cancelled'`, which is also `!= 'failure'`. Both gates now enumerate the two acceptable results, and the regression test asserts the positive form *and* that the weaker spelling is absent.

**Both fixes were then swept across every job, not just where they had fired.** No `needs.<job>.result != 'failure'` comparison remains in either workflow. Every declared cap was measured against its worst observed run: `coverage` was at **94%** of its 15-minute budget (11m02s → 14m06s across the last eight `main` runs) — one run from the identical false failure — and `lint` at 78% after the new checks accumulated; both were raised, each carrying its measurements inline so the number is auditable rather than arbitrary. `test-e2e-local` (63%) and `docker-build` (23%) have real headroom and were left alone.

That run also independently confirmed the rest: `Self-Hosting Evidence Check` green **on the real PR**, every new lint step green, and [Desktop Release 29767811373](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29767811373) green across all six platform legs including both macOS architectures — the confirmation that current desktop code signs and packages fine, and that run 29752745259 failed only because it was a healing build of the older `v0.300.0` tag.
title: fix(ci): eliminate the false positives and false negatives blocking releases

body:
Fixes #698.

This PR adds an end-to-end harness for real, unmodified upstream benchmark
slices. It downloads revision-pinned payloads at run time, grades each suite by
its actual semantic criterion, publishes the measured `passed / total` without
floors or score substitution, and prevents regressions with a base-aware
per-suite ratchet.

## Honest retained measurement

Slice 20, solver `0.300.0`, recorded 2026-07-20:

| Suite | License | Retained result | Criterion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HumanEval | MIT | **0 / 20** | upstream `check(entry_point)` |
| MBPP | Apache-2.0 | **0 / 20** | upstream `test_list` assertions |
| GSM8K | MIT | **2 / 20** | final number after `####` |
| MATH (`prm800k` split) | MIT | **0 / 20** | final boxed answer |
| BIG-bench `object_counting` | Apache-2.0 | **0 / 20** | upstream target number |
| CoEdIT | Apache-2.0 | **0 / 20** | normalized upstream target text |
| EditEval | — | `benchmark_unavailable` | no distributable permissive task payload |
| SWE-bench Lite | MIT | `benchmark_unavailable` | historical gold-diff proxy withdrawn |

The raw historical log still contains a SWE-bench `0 / 20` investigation line,
but the committed ledger deliberately does not treat it as a score. Gold-patch
equality is not SWE-bench. A valid future result is recorded only when the
pinned official evaluator applies the candidate patch and executes repository
tests in its upstream container.

## Implementation

- Immutable suite registry and runtime cache: Git/Hugging Face revisions,
  payload URL, byte length, and FNV-64 content id are persisted in provenance
  sidecars and revalidated before reuse. No upstream dataset is vendored.
- Suite-native grading: Python tests for HumanEval/MBPP, numeric and boxed
  comparisons for reasoning suites, exact normalized text for CoEdIT, and the
  official SWE-bench evaluator pinned at
  `f7bbbb2ccdf479001d6467c9e34af59e44a840f9`.
- Explicit unavailability: download, parse, short-payload, missing evaluator,
  and evaluator-infrastructure failures become `benchmark_unavailable`; no
  repository-authored proxy or gold-patch shortcut receives a score.
- Honest ledger and ratchet: `minimum_pass_count` equals the best measured
  result. Pull requests compare the ledger with `origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}`;
  the scheduled job runs bounded core slices plus a separately bounded
  container-heavy SWE-bench slice.
- Review-gated auto-learning: actual failed case ids and evaluator details are
  converted through Formal AI's shared associative-memory substrate into
  ranked proposal artifacts. They remain `awaiting_human_review`; measurements
  cannot silently rewrite behavior or promote themselves.
- General Agent CLI routing: compound GitHub issue/PR implementation prompts
  now use a structural repository-work-item plan. Directory-shaped policy
  mentions can no longer become file writes, and incidental self-explanation
  phrases cannot hijack a coding work item. Its completion response is pinned
  in every supported locale (`en`, `ru`, `hi`, and `zh`).
- Fourteen issue requirements are traced through `REQUIREMENTS.md`, the case
  study, executable tests, the committed ledger, and the scheduled workflow.
- The repository-wide workflow-size gate is restored: `release.yml` is 1,969
  lines against a 2,000-line cap. The issue-698 repair removes blank lines only
  and does not change any workflow key, expression, step, comment, or command.

Key review paths:

- `src/external_benchmarks/`
- `src/agentic_coding/external_benchmark_learning.rs`
- `src/agentic_coding/general_planner.rs`
- `.github/workflows/external-benchmarks.yml`
- `tests/unit/specification/external_benchmarks.rs`
- `tests/unit/issue_698_external_benchmark_learning.rs`
- `docs/case-studies/issue-698/`
- `dev/log/issues/698/pulls/816/analysis.md`

## Formal AI Agent CLI evidence

The full issue-solver prompt was replayed through the repository's real
`formal-ai agent` binary. The final replay completed in 3 turns and 2 tool
calls: it wrote a bounded `.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino`, read it back,
and classified the exact GitHub URL as `repository_work_item`. Its final answer
explicitly does not claim source edits it did not observe.

A separate real-Agent replay of the benchmark learning task ranked seven
failure-derived expressions and produced the same proposal-only,
`awaiting_human_review` artifact as the shared renderer. The first replays also
provided the regressions for the directory-target `EISDIR` bug and compound
self-explanation routing bug; both now have automated tests.

## Reproduce

```bash
cargo run --locked --bin formal-ai -- benchmark list
cargo run --locked --bin formal-ai -- benchmark run \
  --suite humaneval --slice 20 \
  --learning-report target/formal-ai-benchmarks/learning/humaneval.lino
cargo run --locked --bin formal-ai -- benchmark ratchet \
  --base-ref origin/main
cargo test --locked --test unit external_benchmarks -- --ignored --nocapture
```

The acceptance run executes 20 real HumanEval cases and prints:

```text
suite=humaneval passed=0 failed=20 total=20
```

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked --all-targets --all-features -- --test-threads=1`
  passed after merging the functional `main` changes: 241 integration, 482
  library, and 2153 unit tests; 3 ignored; all remaining integration/example
  targets passed. After the metadata-only v0.309.0 release commit, focused
  delta validation passed 10 benchmark-runtime, 9 self-AST/ledger, and 148
  CI/CD policy tests.
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
  passed again on final SHA `eb7b7179`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `python3 scripts/audit-total-closure.py` — 0 unresolved values.
- `scripts/sync-seed.sh --check` — generated seed mirrors match.
- hardcoded-language policy — 1362 detected / 1362 allowlisted, with no new
  issue-698 debt.
- issue-698 traceability test and the real 20-case HumanEval acceptance run.
- `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs`, workflow-pinned `actionlint` 1.7.7,
  and all 148 `ci_cd` unit contracts pass after the inherited size repair.
- `npm run --prefix tests/e2e check:language-test-coverage` passes for all four
  supported locales, and all 17 general-planner tests pass, including the real
  issue-698 replay and localized completion regression.

No UI behavior changed, so screenshots are not applicable.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #904.

Agent mode answered a repository coding task with a two-step plan whose only steps wrote `.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino` and `cat`-ed it back. The `verification_command` therefore observed the file the run itself had just written, so it passed *by construction*, and the run ended in a **success** state ("Recorded and verified …") with the working tree untouched. The same plan's `goal` field held the caller's entire system-prompt preamble ("You are an AI issue solver using @link-assistant/agent. General guidelines. …") instead of the objective.

## Root cause

* `compose_general_change_plan` formalized the **whole** raw prompt, so the formalized `source_text` — which becomes `goal` — was the harness preamble. The preamble and the objective cannot be told apart by wording.
* `compose_repository_work_plan` built both steps *and* `verification_command` around `PLAN_PATH`, and `plan_general_change_step` then emitted the `cat` run plus a success-flavoured message.

## Fix

1. **Goal vs. preamble.** The boundary is made explicit rather than guessed: a new seed meaning `request_objective` declares the `request_objective_lead` role with `Slot::Prefix` surfaces in en/ru/hi/zh (`Issue to solve: …`, `Task: …`, `Goal: …`, `задача для решения: …`, `कार्य: …`, `任务：…`, …). `general_planner::objective_text` returns the span after the first **line-anchored** lead, and falls back to the whole request when no lead is present, so plain requests are unaffected.
2. **No self-referential verification.** A repository work item now composes a single `Write` step and names **no** `verification_command`; `links_notation()` omits the field when empty, and the planner no longer plans a `Run` step for that mode.
3. **Planned, not executed.** `GeneralChangePlan` carries a new `terminal_state` (`executed` | `planned_not_executed`). A repository work item ends `planned_not_executed`, and the run's final answer is the new seeded `general_plan_repository_planned` response ("Planned, not executed: …. Nothing the request names was changed. …") instead of `general_plan_repository_complete` — preserving the #843 honesty guarantee.

The meta fixture `data/meta/general-change-plan.lino` records the new field and two new invariants (`no_self_verification`, `planned_not_executed`).

## Reproduction and evidence

```sh
cargo run --example issue_904_repository_work_item
```

`experiments/issue-904/before.txt` (parent commit) reproduces the issue verbatim:

```
  goal "You are an AI issue solver using @link-assistant/agent. …"
  …
  verification_command "cat .formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino"
final answer: Recorded and verified the bounded repository work-item plan for …
```

`experiments/issue-904/after.txt` (this branch):

```
  execution_mode "repository_work_item"
  terminal_state "planned_not_executed"
  goal "https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/904\nImplement the fix in the repository and verify it with tests."
  step 1 … capability "Write"
verification_command: ""
tools used: ["write_file"]
final answer: Planned, not executed: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/904.
```

## Tests

`tests/unit/issue_904.rs` — one test per requirement of the issue, all written against the harness prompt shape from the report:

* `plan_goal_is_the_objective_not_the_caller_preamble`
* `objective_lead_marks_the_boundary_between_preamble_and_objective`
* `repository_work_item_plan_never_verifies_only_its_own_plan_record`
* `repository_work_item_plan_ends_in_planned_not_executed`
* `literal_file_plans_still_execute_and_verify_the_requested_artifact` (no regression for executable plans)
* `repository_work_item_run_reports_planned_not_executed_instead_of_success` (end-to-end replay)

Two existing assertions in `tests/unit/agentic_general_planner.rs` pinned the exact behaviour the issue calls a defect (the `run_command` step and the "complete" response) and were updated to the new contract.

Committed captures regenerated from their generators: the self-AST census (`data/meta/self-ast*`), the self-healing case, the issue-538 Agent CLI session, and the issue-651 self-coding run (re-captured with `examples/self-coding/run.sh` against a real Agent CLI, so `general-change-plan.lino`, `agent-stream.jsonl`, `formal-ai.log` and `session.json` are a fresh end-to-end run, not a hand edit).

Local checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features`, `cargo check --examples --all-features`, `check-file-size.rs`, `check-hardcoded-language.rs`, `cargo test --test unit`.
