Fixes https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/931

## Summary

- add localhost-default WebSocket and WebRTC data-channel adapters around the existing transport-neutral OpenAI-compatible router
- add a `formal-ai connect` client so the same binary operates both ends of either transport
- preserve shared authorization, memory, model routing, and agent mode without introducing storage, STUN, TURN, or a relay
- document the protocols, library tradeoffs, root cause, self-hosting evidence, and release metadata

## Reproduction

Before this change, the release binary rejected all three requested surfaces with Clap exit status 2:

```console
formal-ai --silent serve --ws       # unexpected argument '--ws'
formal-ai --silent serve --webrtc   # unexpected argument '--webrtc'
formal-ai --silent connect          # unrecognized subcommand 'connect'
```

The complete pre-fix output is preserved in `docs/case-studies/issue-931/raw-data/repro-before.log`.

After this change:

```bash
formal-ai serve --ws
formal-ai connect --transport websocket --endpoint 127.0.0.1:8080 --prompt 'Hi'

formal-ai serve --webrtc
formal-ai connect --transport webrtc --endpoint 127.0.0.1:8080 --prompt 'Привет'
```

## Design and security

Both adapters serialize the method, path, headers, and body into one request envelope and invoke `handle_api_request_with_headers`, the same router used by HTTP. The response preserves status, content type, body, and deprecation metadata.

WebRTC uses reliable ordered data channels, host ICE candidates, 12 KiB chunks, and bounded local TCP offer/answer signaling. It configures no STUN or TURN service and no central relay. Payload and signaling frames are capped at 16 MiB. All modes default to `127.0.0.1:8080`; bearer-token checks remain in the shared permission layer. `--transport-trace` adds opt-in lifecycle diagnostics and is off by default.

## Verification

- `cargo test --all-features --test integration issue_931_local_transports -- --nocapture` — 2 passed
- `cargo test --all-features --test unit issue_931_local_transport_contract -- --nocapture` — 3 passed
- `cargo test --all-features --test unit issue_673_self_ast_census -- --test-threads=1` — 8 passed
- `cargo test --all-features --test unit issue_538_traceability -- --test-threads=1` — passed
- `cargo check --examples --all-features`
- `cargo test --doc --verbose`
- `npm run test:web`
- `cargo clippy --all-features --lib --bins --tests -- -D warnings`
- formatting, hardcoded-language, file-size, tests-as-docs, dependency-lock, changelog, version, requirement-assembly, CI-registry, PR-link, and self-hosting policy checks

The integration regression starts real HTTP, WebSocket, and WebRTC subprocesses. It proves 401 authorization parity, shared-memory writes, full WebRTC offer/answer, same-binary server/client operation, English/Russian/Hindi/Chinese answer byte parity with HTTP, a 20 KiB request, and an API response larger than 16 KiB.

The exact documented `websocat 1.14.1` command was also run manually and returned the expected status-200 greeting while writing memory; its output is in `docs/case-studies/issue-931/raw-data/manual-websocat.log`.

A repository-wide serial test run reached the newly added self-AST/traceability assertions after 2,727 passing unit tests. Those three generated-contract failures were corrected, and all affected regressions pass in focused reruns. Eight pre-existing socket-timeout failures from the initial parallel run also pass when rerun serially. Fresh GitHub Actions at the final pushed SHA provide the clean sharded full-suite verification.

## Self-hosting and evidence

The real Formal AI Agent CLI authored one of five smallest implementation leaves: the canonical local-transport protocol contract. The session, complete logs, decomposition, and byte-identical artifact are preserved under `docs/case-studies/issue-931/self-hosting-authorship/`. The issue case study and raw GitHub evidence are under `docs/case-studies/issue-931/`; PR-specific CI and review evidence are under `docs/case-studies/pull-request-1008/`.

This is a native protocol and CLI change with no visual UI changes, so screenshots and visual regression tests are not applicable.

## Summary

Fixes #442 — CI ran the full Rust test suite on changes that touch **no code at all** (docs-only commits, `.gitkeep` edits, changelog-fragment-only commits), wasting runner time and slowing iteration.

### Root cause

The `test` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` gated on the wrong signal:

```yaml
if: ... || needs.changelog.result == 'success' || needs.changelog.result == 'skipped'
```

The `changelog` job is itself skipped **precisely when there are no code changes** (`any-code-changed == 'false'`). So the chain was:

```
no code changed → changelog SKIPPED → needs.changelog.result == 'skipped' is TRUE → test RUNS
```

`test` was the only change-sensitive job keying off a sibling job's `skipped` *result* instead of the `detect-changes` *outputs` that `lint` and `coverage` use.

**Proof:** [run 27463712189](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/27463712189) ran the full `cargo test` matrix for commit `19a07a58`, whose entire diff was a one-line deletion in `.gitkeep`. In that same run `Lint`, `Coverage`, `E2E`, and `Changelog` all correctly skipped.

### Fix

Decouple `test` from `changelog` and gate it on the change detector (the pattern the **python** template already uses correctly):

```yaml
test:
  needs: [detect-changes]
  if: |
    always() && !cancelled() && (
      github.event_name == 'push' ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.rs-changed == 'true' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.toml-changed == 'true' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
    )
```

Non-code change → `test` skips → `build` (needs lint+test) also skips. Code change / push / dispatch → `test` runs. The changelog *check* itself is unchanged.

### How to verify

- Regression tests in `tests/unit/ci-cd/workflow_release.rs`:
  - `test_job_skips_non_code_changes` — pins the corrected gating, forbids the `needs.changelog.result == 'skipped'/'success'` clauses from returning.
  - `change_gated_jobs_never_depend_on_a_skipped_changelog` — generalizes the invariant to `lint`/`test`/`coverage`/`test-e2e-local`.
- Run: `cargo test --test unit -- ci_cd::workflow_release` → 18 passed.

### Template comparison & upstream reports (issue requirement)

Downloaded all four pipeline templates and compared the `test` gating. **python = correct reference**; **rust / csharp / js share the bug** (rust is the direct source of this repo's pipeline). Reported upstream with reproducible example + workaround + fix:

- rust: link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#71
- csharp: link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#25
- js: link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#79

### Case study

`docs/case-studies/issue-442/` — downloaded logs/data, reconstructed timeline, full requirement list, root-cause analysis, solution plan, prior-art survey (`dorny/paths-filter`, native `paths` filters), and the upstream report links.

### Notes

- Existing detector tracing (`scripts/detect-code-changes.rs`) was already sufficient to confirm the root cause from the run log, so no extra verbose mode was needed; the new tests make the invariant executable instead.

Fixes #442
title: fix(ci): stop running the test suite on non-code changes (#442)

("turn here and you'll learn the current topics `<Google Trends URL>`") was
answered with `intent: unknown`. The maintainer then widened the ambition: the
engine should have automated tools that convert a live source like Google Trends
into the auto-learning process, in every supported language, and the *same*
teaching directive should be executable through Formal AI's own Agent CLI.

This PR makes that directive a first-class, language-agnostic **`learn_from_source`**
intent that drives two entry points through one seed-declared registry — with no
production branch on any specific URL or phrase.

- **Data-driven registry.** `data/seed/learning-sources.lino` declares each
  learnable `source` (its `capability`, `host`, and native-language `keyword`s)
  plus shared, language-agnostic `directive` cues. Adding a new learnable source
  is a seed edit, never a code change.
- **Single source of truth.** `src/seed.rs::LearningSources::match_directive`
  matches only when a lowercased prompt carries **both** a directive cue and a
  reference to a declared source. Both entry points call it, so recognition can
  never drift between chat and the Agent CLI.
- **Chat entry point.** `src/solver_handlers/mod.rs::try_learn_from_source`
  routes the directive to `intent "learn_from_source"`, localized to the prompt's
  language, and reports the auto-learning coverage split. It declines (no answer)
  for a capability with no wired learning loop.
- **Agent CLI drives the same words.** `is_google_trends_learning_task` now
  recognizes the seed-driven directive, so `run_agentic_task(<reported prompt>)`
  walks `write_file → run_command(verify) → final` and writes the committed
  `data/meta/google-trends-learning.lino` learning report. The session is pinned
  byte-for-byte and driven **live in CI** through the real external Agent CLI.
- **Feeds the gated loop, adopts nothing.** Both entry points route the Google
  Trends learning frontier (60 of 80 catalog prompts) through the human-gated
  issue-#558 self-improvement learner. Trending searches are open-domain
  questions, not program-plan modifiers, so nothing is auto-adopted — the value
  is the auditable frontier.

## Reproduction

```sh
# Chat: the reported directive now routes instead of returning intent: unknown
cargo test --test unit -- issue_499_learn_from_source --nocapture

# Agent CLI: the same teaching directive drives the learning recipe
cargo run --example issue_499_dump_agent_cli_session

# Real external Agent CLI ↔ live formal-ai serve (also run in CI):
TASK="Here you can learn the trending topics from Google Trends: https://trends.google.com/trending/rss?geo=US" \
EXPECT_FILE=google-trends-learning.lino EXPECT_TEXT=human_gated MIN_POSTS=3 PORT=8772 \
  experiments/agent_cli_e2e/run_agent_cli.sh
```

## Tests

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` (clean)
- `cargo test` — full suite green (unit 1463 passed / 2 ignored, doc 71, source 475)
- `tests/unit/issue_499_learn_from_source.rs` — pins the exact reported prompt,
  language-agnostic routing (en/ru/hi/zh) with localized acknowledgement,
  cue-plus-source requirement, the Agent CLI recipe write, and the byte-for-byte
  pinned session.
- `tests/unit/docs_requirements_issue_499.rs` — case-study/documentation
  traceability (`issue_499_learn_from_source_documents_are_traceable`).
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — real Agent CLI E2E step drives the directive
  end-to-end (canary `human_gated`).

## Case study

[`docs/case-studies/issue-499/`](docs/case-studies/issue-499/README.md) — collected
issue/PR/research data, requirements (R499-1…R499-8), per-requirement solution
plan, the pinned Agent CLI session, and the captured live E2E run log.
title: Recognize the #499 learn-from-source directive and drive it via the Agent CLI

## Summary

- preserve explicit tool failure metadata across OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, and Responses inputs
- separate observed attempts from successful planner steps, recover one rejected write with read + bounded retry, preserve the primary write when an auxiliary plan write fails, and stop honestly on repeated or verification failures
- require successful verification output to match the requested bytes before reporting completion
- seed mismatch/unverified responses in all five supported languages and refresh generated closure/self-AST evidence

Closes #905.

## Reproduction and root cause

The reported prompt, `Create a file hello.txt containing exactly: Hello World`, reproduced three defects: the shorter equal-start marker left `exactly:` in the payload; provider error metadata was discarded while every tool result counted as completed; and the general planner emitted success based on call counts without checking result status or output.

The pre-fix focused suite retained in `docs/case-studies/issue-905/test-evidence/regression-red.log` fails 6 of 7 assertions. Both original Agent CLI provider traces and authenticated issue/PR snapshots are retained in the case study. This is a protocol/state bug, so no visual screenshot applies.

## Relationship to `main`

While this branch was open, `main` landed its own fixes for the three defects named in the original issue text: `strip_clause_lead` in `src/agentic_coding/general_planner.rs` (control-phrase parsing) and `ShellEnvelope`/`failed_verification` in `src/agentic_coding/tool_result.rs` (exit-code-aware failure reporting). Those implementations are kept as-is by this merge; the branch's earlier, narrower versions were dropped.

What remains unique to this pull request is the requirement added by the qwen trace in the issue comment — `is_error: true` tool results were being discarded entirely, so the plan advanced over a step that never ran:

- `ChatMessage::is_error` on the shared protocol type, populated from Anthropic `tool_result.is_error`, Responses `is_error`/`isError`/failed `status`, and the OpenAI-compatible `is_error`/`isError` fields
- `Progress` recording observed attempts separately from satisfied steps, so a rejected call cannot count as progress
- the two-turn `read_file` → `write_file` recovery the issue comment asked for, bounded per target path
- content-match verification: literal completion compares transport-normalized command output against the request-derived payload
- `general_execution.rs`, the plan's execution state machine, split out of the planner

## Verification

Latest run, on `06d5a9e2`, which merges `origin/main` (`52ef42e7`, v0.333.0) into the branch:

- `cargo test --test unit` — 2574 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored
- `cargo test --test integration -- --test-threads=1` — 306 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (serialized to respect the local runner's socket limit)
- `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `scripts/audit-total-closure.py` — `UNRESOLVED distinct: 0  occurrences: 0`
- `check-file-size`, `check-associative-terminology`, `check-hardcoded-language`, `check-disk-usage-policy`, `check-worker-line-budget`, `check-changelog-fragment` — all passed
- CI on the merged head `06d5a9e2`: CI/CD Pipeline, Coverage, Write-Effect Ladder, Task Ladder, Agentic CLI Matrix, Agent CLI E2E, External Benchmarks, Desktop Release — all eight green

Generated artifacts (self-AST census, planner fixtures, total-closure shards) were regenerated from the merged sources, so they remain pure functions of `src/**` and `data/seed/**`.

Regression coverage includes the exact prompt, 20 parsing variants, Qwen-style explicit errors, Codex-style nonzero exits, bounded write recovery, wrong/matching verification evidence, requested failure vocabulary, and Anthropic/Responses parity. Acceptance traceability is in `docs/case-studies/issue-905/requirements.md`.

## Merge with `main` (v0.333.0)

`main` advanced repeatedly while this branch was open, and each time the pull request went conflicted the conflicts were confined to *generated* artifacts — `data/meta/self-ast/index.lino` and the `data/seed/closure-generated-*.lino` shards. None was ever resolved by hand: `main`'s side was taken and then both artifact families were regenerated from the merged sources (`cargo run --example regenerate_self_ast_census`, `python3 scripts/close-total.py`), so the committed bytes remain exactly what the generators produce. No source file has conflicted at any point.

The final merge (`06d5a9e2`, bringing in `52ef42e7` / v0.333.0) had a single conflict, in `data/meta/self-ast/index.lino`, resolved the same way. The branch is now `MERGEABLE` against `main`.

## The completion claim is now seeded, not English in Rust

The sentence this issue quotes as the false report — `Completed the general change request for … and verified it with …` — was the last outcome of the general-change state machine still typed into `src/` as an English literal, while every failure path (`general_plan_unverified`, `general_plan_verification_mismatch`, `general_plan_repository_planned`) already resolved through the seed. That contradicted the repository's meanings ↔ naturalization rule: a Russian or Chinese request that *succeeded* was answered in English, while the same request that *failed* was answered in its own language.

`general_plan_completed` is now a seeded intent in all five supported languages, rendered through `localized_response`. The English text is byte-identical, so every existing assertion is unchanged; `scripts/hardcoded-language-allowlist.txt` loses exactly one entry, and the five-language response test now covers the completion claim alongside the two failure intents.

## Same-task self-application

Formal AI served the `formal-ai` model to the external Agent CLI in session `ses_034e9dafeffe7nxeTkFhmHLmZN`, which authored and read back the canonical tool-result evidence invariant. That is 1 of 5 reviewed smallest leaves (20%). Session `ses_03474fd81ffeMofsJrUWdYDEEd` refreshed the planner-derived self-healing fixture through the same real client/server path. Replay harnesses and byte-identical artifacts are retained under `experiments/issue_905_*` and `docs/case-studies/issue-905/`.

An earlier whole-issue attempt selected an unsupported hosted fallback and received HTTP 401 before Formal AI executed. It is retained as failed infrastructure evidence and is not counted as authorship; echoed authorization headers are redacted.


## Write-effect ladder regression (fixed)

The issue #916 write-effect ladder, which `main` added while this branch was open, failed rung R916-01 on the first push of the merged branch: `dishonest report=['reported failure although every declared effect landed']`, baseline 9/9 → 8/9.

Root cause: R916-01 replays the exact issue #905 transport fault (`write_stdin failed: Unknown process id 0`, bytes never land). This branch's recovery path exhausted its bounded per-path retries and then reported the transport message directly, without ever running the check the plan itself had named — so the run ended in a failure report that no observed exit code backed.

Fix: once write recovery is exhausted, run the named verification once; its exit status is what the report carries. Locally the ladder is back to 9/9 (`baseline 9/9 -> now 9/9`), and `an_unrecoverable_write_still_asks_the_workspace_before_reporting` pins the behavior in the unit suite.
title: Require tool-result evidence before general-change completion

## What & why

Closes the remaining items of #819. Merged PR #830 already fixed `find`
routing, the localized not-found message, and the report multiselect. This PR
addresses the follow-up the user filed on the reported OpenCode session:

> there is no need to print the command that will be executed in the message
> before it, Formal AI just needs to explain what it is about to do, and command
> anyway printed by OpenCode itself when actually executed.
>
> `so I can verify the next step before continuing.` does not produce any
> meaningful information … it is not robotic but actually useful and natural.

### Before (reported)

```
I'll use bash on find "${FORMAL_AI_DESKTOP_DIR:-$HOME/Desktop}" -type d \( -iname 'hive*mind*control*center*' … so I can verify the next step before continuing.
$ find "${FORMAL_AI_DESKTOP_DIR:-$HOME/Desktop}" -type d …
```

### After (matches how `claude` / `codex` phrase the same request)

```
Let me look on your Desktop for hive-mind-control center folder.
```

The narration now never echoes the command — OpenCode prints it itself when the
step runs. Each capability gets a natural, spoken sentence in every supported
language (en/ru/hi/zh), the robotic tail is gone, and the empty-result and
report steps read plainly for a beginner.

## Changes

- **`fix(agentic)`** — capability-aware, command-free narration selected from
  the seed catalog (`tool_action_narration`); local path lookups get a
  location-aware sentence built from the same extraction the `find` builder uses.
- **`refactor(seed)`** — the natural `agentic_action_*` phrases live in a new
  `data/seed/multilingual-responses-agentic.lino`, walked alongside the main
  catalog via `RESPONSE_FILES`, keeping both under the 1,500-line seed guard.
- **`test(agentic)`** — the whole OpenCode journey (find → empty result →
  report → multiselect → combined action) is driven end to end through the real
  HTTP API in `tests/integration/issue_819_report_flow.rs`, plus narration e2e
  across the HTTP and typed-solver paths, and per-language narration pinned in
  `tests/unit/issue_819_narration.rs` (en/ru/hi/zh).
- **`docs(contributing)`** — recommends spawning a free `claude`/`codex`/
  `opencode` model on the identical prompt to calibrate natural-language tone.

## Self-hosting evidence

The user-facing fix is hand-authored maintenance, committed **without**
self-authorship trailers per `CONTRIBUTING.md`. To keep the differential
self-hosting ratchet honest on the branch, this PR also records a genuine piece
of Formal-AI-authored release work under
`docs/case-studies/issue-819/self-hosting-evidence/`: the system's own
whole-repository source-to-links projection (issue #558's "translate the entire
source of our system to links and back" recipe), driven through the real Agent
CLI against a locally-served, memory-isolated Formal AI
(`experiments/issue-819-self-hosting-evidence/run.sh`, session
`ses_0702a074dffeiWQoNMe5nRv35f`).

Both recorded artifacts are deterministic, byte-for-byte reproducible functions
of the embedded source tree (no neural inference):

- `self-source-links.lino` / `session.json` — what the agentic loop recorded
  through the Agent CLI (the responsive representative-slice projection).
- `whole-repository-projection-NN.lino` — the exhaustive full-fidelity
  projection: `SourceLinks::owned()` translating every one of the 292 owned
  modules to Links Notation and back, each proven to round-trip byte-for-byte.
  It is **sharded** into independently-valid Links Notation trees, each under
  the 1,500-line `.lino` ceiling (`scripts/check-file-size.rs`), exactly as
  `scripts/close-total.py` shards its generated closure. The new
  `examples/project_source_links_sharded.rs` writes and asserts the shards.

The Agent CLI transcript (`agent-stream.jsonl`) and server trace
(`formal-ai.log`) are the excluded evidence bundle binding the artifacts to the
session id.

## How it was verified

- Full suite: **2700 passed, 0 failed** (`cargo test --all`).
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --examples --release -- -D warnings`
  clean.
- Self-hosting: trailer validation exit 0 (41.37 %, 2161/5224 changed lines);
  `--check-ratchet origin/main` reports **"self-hosting ratchet holds"** (exit 0).
- File-size guard, hardcoded-language guard, and changelog-fragment guard all
  exit 0; every `.lino` shard is within the 1,500-line limit.
- Language guards (`check:i18n`, `check:language-parity`,
  `check:language-test-coverage`, `check:intent-coverage`) pass for en/ru/hi/zh.
- Narration compared against `claude` and `codex` transcripts on the reported
  prompt (see issue #819 screenshots) — the shipped phrasing matches their
  natural, command-free shape.

## Reproduce

```bash
cargo test --test integration issue_819_report_flow
cargo test --test integration issue_819_narration
cargo test --test unit issue_819_narration
# Regenerate the sharded whole-repository projection (byte-for-byte stable):
cargo run --release --example project_source_links_sharded -- \
  docs/case-studies/issue-819/self-hosting-evidence
```



Fixes #819

body:
Closes #701.

E59 said the auto-learning loop never closed: it *observed* its failures and stopped. Two symptoms were named, and both were real when measured.

**Symptom 1 — the Trends frontier never moved.** 60 of the 80 committed Google Trends prompts (10 topics × 4 languages × 2 variations) came back `intent: unknown`, run after run, with nothing derived from them.

**Symptom 2 — dreaming amendments were decoration.** `examples/issue_701_amendment_body.rs` reproduces it: solve a prompt plainly, solve it again with a matching retained amendment, strip the appended compliance line, diff the bodies.

```
--- latex: solve a new recurrence proof
plain intent   = unknown
amended intent = unknown
body differs beyond the appended line = false
```

Root cause: `solve_with_amendment_records` prepends a `Standing requirement (...)` user turn, `solve_with_history` records it as a `prior_turn:user` event, and **no downstream handler ever reads it**. The rule reached the log and the prose, never the routing.

## What this PR does

### 1. An adoption contract (R701-1)

`formal-ai learn cycle --frontier google-trends --dry-run [--proposals]` runs one cycle:

```
frontier item → candidate surface → held-out validation → promotion proposal (#656 shape)
```

Candidates are **request-opener surfaces** generalized from ≥2 distinct terms — `… के बारे में बताओ`, `介绍一下 …`, `Дай контекст Google Trends для …` — so a candidate can never be a memorized single prompt. Each is replayed against held-out prompts built from terms it was *not* derived from; one that fails is recorded as blocked, not dropped. One recorded run: 60 frontier items → 6 candidates → 6 validated → 48 held-out tests → 2 proposals. Deterministic and offline.

### 2. Proof of capability delta (R701-2)

`data/meta/learning-adoption-ledger.lino` — **60 before/after pairs, 10 topics, 4 languages**:

```
adoption_pair
  topic "julián andrés quiñones"
  language "en"
  before_intent "unknown"
  before_routed_to "human_triage"
  after_intent "web_search"
  after_query "julián andrés quiñones"
  topic_recovered "true"
  capability_delta "unknown_to_web_search"
```

Tool-authored (`cargo run --release --example issue_701_adoption_ledger`) and byte-pinned against a fresh render.

### 3. The Trends gap, closed (R701-3)

| Measure | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Routed by the engine | 20 | **80** |
| On the learning frontier | 60 | **0** |
| `intent: unknown` rate | 7500 bp | **0 bp** |

Ratcheted by `the_trends_corpus_unknown_rate_is_ratcheted_to_zero`. The 60 pre-adoption verdicts stay frozen in `data/meta/learning-frontier-google-trends.lino` — the gap closing does not erase the evidence it existed.

### 4. The decoration-only path, deleted (R701-4)

A retained standing requirement now changes how a task is **classified**, which a string append cannot do: a covered task the solver could not otherwise route is no longer returned as unresolved, and it cites the amendment as evidence. The three application paths (solver, memory recall, agentic final) were collapsed onto one selection rule (`matching_amendments`) and one projection (`amendment_lines`); the duplicated `matching_amendment_lines` decorator is gone.

`tests/unit/issue_701_dreaming_amendment_class.rs` raises the single-prompt #540 check into a class:

- 3 topics × 4 languages of **held-out paraphrases** through both `create_chat_completion_with_solver_and_memory` and `create_response_with_solver_and_memory`;
- a covered task is never reported unresolved;
- a **negative control** — an uncovered task must come back byte-identical to the empty-memory answer, so "the answer changed" is evidence of something.

### 5. Periodic, proposal-only, human-gated (R701-5)

- In-process: every idle dreaming run writes a learning-cycle record next to the memory log.
- Scheduled CI: `.github/workflows/learning-cycle.yml` runs daily, publishes proposals as an artifact, and asserts `mode "proposal_only"`, `human_gated "true"`, and `git diff --exit-code -- data/seed`. A cycle that stops proposing anything fails the job rather than passing quietly.

### 6. Durable failure records (R701-6)

Frozen frontier record plus blocked classes in the cycle record; nothing is silently dropped (R425).

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Result |
| --- | --- |
| ≥1 valid promotion proposal with tests, deterministic and offline | 2 proposals, 6 validated candidates, 48 held-out tests |
| Ledger ≥20 pairs / ≥3 topics / 4 languages | 60 pairs, 10 topics, 4 languages |
| Regression test on a **held-out paraphrase** | `retained_amendments_change_held_out_answers_across_topics_and_languages` (12 paraphrases, both surfaces) |
| `intent: unknown` rate drops and is ratcheted | 7500 bp → 0 bp, ratcheted |

## Honest narrowings

- The cycle derives one *class* of knowledge — request-opener surfaces — because that is the class the recorded frontier actually consists of. The contract is class-agnostic; the tested coverage is not, and we do not claim otherwise.
- Requirement 4's delta is a change in routing and evidence, not a rewrite of the answer body by the standing rule. A deterministic engine cannot invent a body from a rule it has no handler for; claiming it did would be the decoration problem in a new costume.

## Merge integration and verification

Merged `main` at release `v0.312.0`. The integration exposed and fixed two concrete mainline interactions:

- the added learning subcommand pushed `src/main.rs` over its hard 1,000-line gate, so learning argument parsing and dispatch now live together in `src/cli_learn.rs` and the self-AST census was regenerated;
- the `v0.312.0` release consumed issue #844's changelog fragment, while its traceability test still required the deleted pre-release file. The test now follows the repository's established fragment-or-released-`CHANGELOG.md` lifecycle.

The first exact-merge CI run also exposed two independent stability bugs, both reproduced before fixing:

- macOS ARM64 packaging completed signing and ZIP creation, then the runner's disk-image service returned `hdiutil: attach failed - Device not configured`. The membership probe now feeds `grep` directly, backed by a deterministic 3,017-name regression test.

## Summary

- Constrain the crates.io package with a `Cargo.toml` `include` allowlist so repository-only docs, tests, scripts, experiments, and case-study artifacts are not uploaded.
- Add `scripts/check-crate-package-size.rs` and run it in the build job after `cargo package --list`, failing before publish if the generated `.crate` archive exceeds the crates.io 10 MiB limit.

The failing release packaged 792 files and produced a 16.1 MiB compressed `.crate`, then crates.io rejected the upload with HTTP 413 because the max upload size is 10,485,760 bytes. Locally, the pre-fix package reproduced at 805 files and 16,884,863 bytes.

## Fixes #479 — `Not available in latest release` for all desktop apps

Every desktop release since `v0.187.0` shipped **zero** desktop assets, so `/download`
showed *"Not available in latest release"* for macOS, Windows and Linux. This PR fixes the
actual root cause (three coupled CI bugs), replaces the rejected synthetic macOS
screenshots with **genuine** captures, turns the landing "source code" link into a **big
button**, and lands a deep case study under `docs/case-studies/issue-479/`.

This redo follows the maintainer's review on the issue (synthetic screenshots rejected;
source-code must be a big button; "redo analysis"). Everything is in this single PR.

---

### 1. Why desktop apps were unavailable — three coupled root causes

The auto-release job tags a **child** `chore: release vX.Y.Z` commit, but the CI
`workflow_run` that drives the desktop build carries that child's **parent** SHA. Three
independent bugs then each suppressed the desktop build:

| # | Layer | Root cause | Fix |
|---|-------|-----------|-----|
| 1 | `desktop-release.yml` resolve | Required a tag pointing at `workflow_run.head_sha`; the head SHA is the *parent*, never the tagged child → exact-SHA match always failed. | Resolve now targets the **latest published release** with a defensive exact-SHA tier + an **idempotency guard**, and prints grouped `[desktop-release-resolve]` verbose diagnostics. |
| 2 | `desktop-release.yml` gating | Gated on full-pipeline `conclusion == 'success'`. The release is published *early*, so any later job failure suppressed the **whole** desktop build. | Gate no longer requires `conclusion == 'success'` — it runs on any completed `main` pipeline. |
| 3 | `wait-for-pages-deployment.sh` | The E2E Pages probe required the deploy SHA to appear verbatim in the served `index`. New landing/docs pages shipped without cache-busted assets → probe spun 300 s → failed pipeline → gated the release (feeds layer 2). | Probe is now **marker-authoritative**: `deployment.json`'s SHA proves the matching stamped build is live (GitHub Pages deploys atomically). Landing/docs assets are cache-busted with `?v=__FORMAL_AI_ASSET_VERSION__`, like `/app/`. |

Layer 1 alone (merged earlier in #480) was **dormant** — layers 2–3 still suppressed every
build, which is why the issue was *"still not fixed"*. All three are addressed here, and the
self-healing resolve clears the asset-less backlog on the first run because `/download` only
ever surfaces the **latest** release.

**Before** (maintainer screenshot, `v0.203.0`): release assets exist for the tag, yet
`/download` still says *"Not available in latest release"* and source-code is a small link —
[`raw-data/maintainer-rejection-screenshot.png`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-479-51f54bbe54b1/docs/case-studies/issue-479/raw-data/maintainer-rejection-screenshot.png?raw=true).

### 2. Real macOS screenshots (not synthetic renders)

The previous attempt drew/generated the macOS Gatekeeper images; the maintainer rejected them
as fake and asked for ones *"copied from our code"* at
[`konard/vk-bot-desktop`](https://github.com/konard/vk-bot-desktop). macOS Gatekeeper **cannot**
be triggered on a hosted macOS CI runner (it only blocks quarantined downloads), so these
**cannot** be regenerated in CI. Instead the three `/download` figures are now the **genuine**
macOS 15 (Sequoia) captures from the sibling app **VK Bot Desktop**, which ships the
**identical** `electron-builder` ad-hoc signing flow (`CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false`, no
Apple Developer ID — exactly what `desktop-release.yml` does here). The dialogs are
byte-identical for `formal-ai Desktop`; **only the app name in the prompt differs**, and the
localized `alt`/caption copy says so.

The synthetic generator (`tests/e2e/scripts/generate-macos-screenshots.mjs`) and its HTML
fixture (`tests/e2e/fixtures/macos-gatekeeper.html`) are **removed**. Provenance is documented
in `src/web/download/assets/screenshots/README.md`, and the served PNGs are **byte-identical**
(verified by SHA-256) to the upstream captures mirrored at
`docs/case-studies/issue-479/raw-data/vk-bot-desktop-current/macos-screenshots/`.

![Real macOS Gatekeeper "Not Opened" capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-479-51f54bbe54b1/src/web/download/assets/screenshots/macos-gatekeeper-not-opened.png?raw=true)

[`/download` install section rendered with the real captures](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-479-51f54bbe54b1/docs/case-studies/issue-479/screenshots/download-macos-real-screenshots.png?raw=true)

### 3. Source code is a big button on the landing page

`/` now surfaces the repository as a prominent `.source-cta` hero button (eyebrow **OPEN
SOURCE** + `</>` icon + **Source on GitHub**), translated for every locale — not the old small
footer link.

![Landing page with the big source button + app/docs/download chooser](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-479-51f54bbe54b1/docs/case-studies/issue-479/screenshots/landing-source-button-light.png?raw=true)

### 4. Site structure

`/` is a localized landing chooser → web app (`/app/`), documentation hub (`/docs/`, with a
generated Rust API reference at `/docs/api/` built by `cargo doc` during the Pages deploy),
and desktop download (`/download/`). The interactive app moved from `/` to `/app/` with
`<base href="../">` so shared assets resolve under both the Pages path-prefix and the desktop
static server.

### 5. Deep case study — `docs/case-studies/issue-479/`

Reconstructs the timeline, every requirement, all three root causes (grounded in the verbatim
resolve-step log, the tag/commit topology, and the captured release-asset evidence), the fix
design, and a reproduction + verification procedure. Raw data includes the verbatim maintainer
rejection comment and a genuine `v0.203.0` screenshot. The
[`template-comparison/REPORT.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-479-51f54bbe54b1/docs/case-studies/issue-479/template-comparison/REPORT.md)
compares the CI/CD against the four `link-foundation` pipeline templates (js/rust/python/csharp).

> **Upstream issues:** the four templates were compared file-by-file. The child-release /
> head-SHA coupling that broke desktop builds here is **specific to this repo's**
> auto-release + desktop-release wiring; **no template shares the bug**, so — per the issue's
> *"if the same issue is found"* condition — **no upstream issues are filed**.

### 6. Tests & verification

- **Unit (Rust):** `cargo test --test unit ci_cd` → **64 passed**. New issue-#479 tests assert
  the relaxed gate (layer 2), the marker-authoritative probe (layer 3) and the `.source-cta`
  big button; `desktop_release_resolve.rs` covers the resolve script across 8 event shapes
  (layer 1). The workflow tests were split into `workflow_release.rs` /
  `release_publishing.rs` / shared `workflow_fixtures.rs` to respect the 1000-line `.rs`
  file-size CI gate.
- **E2E (Playwright):** `tests/issue-479.spec.js` (real screenshots render, load, localized
  alt/caption in en/ru/zh/hi) and `tests/issue-479-site.spec.js` (landing chooser, big source
  button, docs hub).
- **Local lint-job parity (all green):** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets
  --all-features` (`-Dwarnings`), `semantic_grounding`, `check-file-size.rs`, `bun run
  build:web` + vendor-bundle diff, i18n catalog, language-parity, language-test-coverage.

### 7. Release

Two changelog fragments under `changelog.d/` (both `bump: minor`): the structural one is
trimmed to drop the now-superseded claims the maintainer rejected, and the new fragment is the
authoritative record of the three-layer fix, the real captures and the big button.
title: fix(release): make desktop apps available on /download + real macOS screenshots + big source button (#479)

## Summary

- add one seeded software-authoring completion contract shared by Agent, Claude, OpenCode, Codex, Qwen, and Gemini
- require a non-scratch workspace effect before accepting a successful client exit
- escalate through a **seed-declared ladder of recovery strategies** — `restate_postcondition`, `name_target_artifact`, `decompose_into_leaf` — so each retry is a different decomposition rather than a repeat, resuming the native client session when available
- **learn across runs**: every `(client, postcondition, strategy, effect)` triple is appended to a durable ledger outside the caller's workspace, and later runs reorder the ladder to spend what has actually produced artifacts first
- fail closed on public vendor endpoint diversion, now declared in seed data instead of a hardcoded array in `src/`
- emit compact NDJSON with model, endpoint, token, attempt, reason, changed-path, and recovery metadata
- keep `.formal-ai/` scratch state out of completion evidence and Git-visible user changes

## Root cause

`formal-ai with` previously treated the child process exit status as task completion. A client could exit zero after planning, an orientation command, or a no-op response without producing the requested artifact. The wrapper also streamed each client's presentation format directly, so pretty or concatenated JSON was not a stable machine-readable contract.

The earlier revision of this branch closed the gate but retried with a single fixed correction prompt. That is self-healing, not self-learning: a second attempt repeated the same decomposition, and nothing was carried across runs. Issue #879 explicitly asks to "record the (request, plan, outcome) triple and try a different decomposition."

## Generalization

Nothing about the recovery behaviour branches on literals in `src/`:

- the strategy ladder, the attempt budget, the incomplete reason, the scratch directory, and the diverted vendor endpoints are all rows in [`data/seed/client-completion-contracts.lino`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-879-693050b2608b/data/seed/client-completion-contracts.lino)
- each strategy's correction prompt is a seeded multilingual response (`en`, `ru`, `hi`, `zh`), resolved by the detected request language with an English fallback
- adding a fourth strategy, a seventh client, or a new vendor endpoint is a data edit
- learning may only **reorder** the seeded list — it cannot invent, drop, or exceed it, so a missing or corrupted ledger degrades exactly to the seeded order

## Reproduction and automated coverage

The first commit adds a minimal fake Agent CLI that exits zero, emits pretty JSON with empty metadata, and creates no file. It demonstrates the old false-success behavior before the implementation.

`tests/integration/issue_879_completion.rs` verifies:

- zero exit without an artifact is rejected only after the full bounded ladder, and the three corrections escalate through *distinct* instructions
- `recovery_order_is_learned_from_what_actually_produced_artifacts`: a first run teaches that `name_target_artifact` works and `restate_postcondition` does not; a second run sharing the same state directory spends `name_target_artifact` first, the untried strategy next, and the failed one last — while `strategies_available` is unchanged
- the learning ledger resolves outside the workspace and never appears in `git status`
- a correction can resume the exact native Agent session and complete
- the identical Scala task produces `Hello.scala` through all six registered client adapters, each with its editing profile and local Formal AI endpoint
- English, Russian, Hindi, and Chinese authoring prompts all activate the same workspace-effect contract
- every stdout line is independently parseable JSON with populated endpoint and token metadata
- a reported Codex diversion to `api.openai.com` fails closed
- `.formal-ai/` never satisfies the gate or appears in `git status`

## Live end-to-end evidence

Beyond the deterministic fixtures, the ladder ran against the installed Agent CLI and a temporary local Formal AI server in an empty Git repository, with a request the local model could not satisfy. Session `ses_048503119ffe9cCHeMerd8wBVF` spent all three strategies and the wrapper exited nonzero rather than reporting a false success:


## Summary

Closes #563. Generalizes repository summarization from **files only** to **any repository resource — files *and* folders** — by following the meta algorithm's *describe → formalize → decompose → solve → compose* loop, applied recursively over the repository tree.

This addresses the PR review feedback that the file-only surface was "not general enough … what if we want to summarize not only files, but also folders and so on." The meta algorithm must solve any task by description, formalization to the meta language, decomposition, testing, and composition — so summarization now treats a repository as a recursive tree of resources rather than a flat list of files.

## What changed

- **`src/summarization/resource.rs` (new):** the generalization layer.
  - `RepositoryEntry` — a filesystem-free input tree (`File { path, content }` / `Directory { path, children }`), so the layer stays deterministic and testable; a real directory walk builds the tree and hands it in.
  - `formalize_repository_resource` dispatches on kind: files reuse `formalize_repository_file` unchanged; directories recurse through `formalize_repository_directory`, aggregating recursive file/subdirectory counts and total lines/bytes.
  - A folder is summarized by the **decompose → summarize → compose** loop: split the directory into children, summarize each child on its own (files via `file.rs`, subdirectories by recursion), then compose behind an aggregate identity sentence.
  - **Recursion depth is bounded by the summarization mode ladder** (`SummarizationMode::one_step_shorter`), not an ad hoc depth cap: a `Full` folder describes its children in `Standard`, theirs in `Short`, deeper as `Topic`.
  - `summarize_repository_resource` is the single general entry point and reproduces `summarize_repository_file` exactly for file inputs (the file behavior is subsumed, not replaced).
  - `RepositoryDirectoryFormalization::links_notation` renders link-native `repository_directory` evidence.
- **`src/summarization/file.rs`:** exposes `RepositoryFileFormalization::summary` so directory recursion reuses file summaries.
- **Exports** wired through `mod.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, and the `tests/source` mirror.

## How to reproduce / demonstrate

```
cargo run --example issue_563_folder_summary
```

Summarizes a folder tree across `Topic`/`Short`/`Standard`/`Full` modes and prints the `repository_directory` evidence.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/specification/summarization_pipeline.rs`: `summarize_repository_resource_subsumes_file_summarization`, `directory_topic_summary_is_a_single_identity_sentence`, `directory_summary_reports_recursive_aggregate_counts`, `directory_short_summary_bounds_listed_children`, `directory_summary_recurses_with_one_step_shorter_mode`, `formalize_repository_resource_distinguishes_files_and_directories`, `directory_links_notation_lists_children_by_kind` (plus the original file-summary recursion test).
- `tests/source/source_tests/summarization/mod/tests.rs`: matching source-mirror tests for the resource/folder surface.
- `tests/unit/docs_requirements_issue_563.rs`: documentation traceability for R345–R359.

## Docs & traceability

- `REQUIREMENTS.md`: rows **R355–R359** for the folder/resource generalization (alongside R345–R354 for files).
- `docs/case-studies/issue-563/README.md`: new "Generalization From Files To Folders" section, updated requirements table and verification list.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `README.md`: repository-resource (files + folders) summarization described.
- `changelog.d/…issue_563…md`: minor-bump fragment updated.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` (clean), and the full `cargo test` suite all pass locally.

body: Closes #672. PR #542 (issue #541) ended by writing five concrete follow-ups into `docs/case-studies/issue-541/proposed-issues.md`, and none of them was ever filed. This PR treats that file as the specification and lands all five, one commit per item, with the two divergences from the original sketch argued in [`docs/case-studies/issue-672/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-672-e9ff26c1ce11/docs/case-studies/issue-672/README.md) rather than left for a reader to find in the diff. No item was dropped. | Item | What landed | Tests | | --- | --- | --- | | F1 dark-theme regression coverage | computed-colour tables for 5 widgets × 4 theme states × 2 surfaces (web + desktop bridge), plus unasserted review PNGs | `issue-672-theme-snapshots.spec.js` (10) | | F2 migration replay | `DATA_VERSION` 2 adds `Cookies` / `Service Worker` / `WebStorage` / `WebSocketStorage`; `dataMigrationStatus` + `replayDataMigration` carry the result to a renderer notice with a replay button | `issue-672-migration-replay.spec.js` (8) + `desktop/scripts/data-migration.test.mjs` | | F3 animation-budget override | `data-skip-animation` on the message container and a per-message *Show answer now* control; reduced motion still wins without any click | `issue-672-animation-override.spec.js` (11) | | F4 hierarchy editing | right-click menu in Diagnostics mode, backed by an append-only event log projected onto the solver's own labels | `issue-672-reasoning-hierarchy.spec.js` (12) | | F5 IPC mode flip | the #541 R9 grant-all journey re-run with `runAgentProvider` / `setToolGrants` behind a real `page.exposeFunction` boundary | `issue-541-permissions-cold-start.spec.js` (3) | `44 passed (1.7m)` in one run, plus `121/121` desktop node tests. Raw logs are in `docs/case-studies/issue-672/raw-data/`. ## Divergences (both argued in the case study) - **F1 snapshots computed colours, not pixels.** F1's own text recorded why the PNG baselines were not shipped in #542 — repo weight and screenshot flake in CI — and that trade-off has not changed. Snapshotting each widget's computed `color`/`backgroundColor` catches the bug F1 cares about (a widget rendering in the wrong theme's palette), is byte-stable across machines, and diffs in review as text. It also covers more than the sketch asked for: `light`, `dark`, and `auto` under both OS colour schemes, on both surfaces. - **F2 excludes `Cache` and `Code Cache`.** They are derived, they are the largest directories in a profile, and carrying a cache built by a different Chromium build into a fresh profile is a known way to produce hard-to-diagnose corruption. Copying them cannot fix the reported symptom (being logged out). They are named in `EXCLUDED_SUBTREES` with that reasoning inline. - **F5 "server ⇄ embedded" reconciliation.** The item text is about the Chat → Agent flip across the bridge, which is what landed. The server-vs-embedded axis is already covered by `issue-511-cold-start.spec.js`, whose second test runs the same journey against a container-gated commander provider on a real `apiBase`; duplicating it here with a fake `apiBase` would test the fallback rather than the flip. ## Along the way `desktop/scripts/*.test.mjs` was written but never executed by any workflow, so `desktop/lib/data-migration.cjs` — the code that moves a user's whole profile between app names, and that F2 extends — had no gate at all. The Lint job now runs it. The F3/F4 keys pushed `src/web/i18n-catalog.lino` to 1508 lines, past the 1500-line Links Notation limit that `scripts/check-file-size.rs` enforces. The per-locale `message` blocks moved into `src/web/i18n-catalog-messages.lino`, the same way the permission strings were split earlier: the loader fetches every catalog file and merges their per-locale keys, and the catalog-parity, language-change-parity, and language-test-coverage guards all watch the new file. The merged catalog is unchanged — 4 locales and the same 430 keys before and after — and the files are now 912 / 605 / 528 lines. ## Screenshots All of these are written by the specs themselves, so they cannot drift from the code. **F3 — a withheld answer, then the same message after *Show answer now*:** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | **F4 — the thinking preview without `formalize`, the menu, and the preview with the promoted step above an unchanged diagnostics trace:** | Before | Menu | After | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | **F1 — the dark-theme surfaces the colour tables are taken from:** see `docs/screenshots/issue-672/`. ## Reproduction ```bash cd tests/e2e npx playwright test --config playwright.local.config.js issue-672 issue-541-permissions-cold-start cd .. node --test $(ls desktop/scripts/*.test.mjs | grep -v '/web-tools.test.mjs$') ``` Run Playwright from `tests/e2e/`: from the repository root a second `@playwright/test` copy resolves first and the run fails with "Playwright Test did not expect test.describe() to be called here".

Closes #822.

## Summary

- gate reporting behind destination and context confirmation, then persist and export complete agentic exchanges (conversation, tools, metadata, and matching server logs) through shared LiNo-first API/CLI paths
- reconstruct complete transcripts from cumulative or incremental requests plus final and streamed OpenAI, Gemini, and direct responses while preserving physical JSONL order
- add a bounded executable recursive controller: attempt the parent, descend only after failure, extend a failing leaf, retry it, then climb back up and retry the parent
- turn verified symbolic traces in reported conversations into review-gated rule proposals via `learn_rules_from_unknown_traces`
- wire approved `LearningLedger::promote` output into the live solver through cached `lesson_for` recall before fresh unknown-rule synthesis
- document measured self-coding honestly and include a real Formal AI + Agent CLI authored leaf: 1 of the 5 smallest decomposition leaves (20%)

## Root cause

The report planner treated `Report` as an immediate GitHub action and constructed a bounded Markdown summary. Tool inputs/results, harness metadata, server traces, and final streamed responses were not available from one session-keyed source, while complete persistence was opt-in. Incremental histories could lose earlier turns, and timestamp sorting could reorder records sharing a millisecond.

The review follow-up exposed a second gap: the repository described recursive self-improvement, learning, and self-coding as goals, but did not execute the complete loop. Failure did not drive task decomposition, reported traces did not enter rule synthesis, promoted lessons were not recalled by the live solver, and self-coding was measured by changed lines rather than named leaf tasks.

## Implementation

Reporting now uses two confirmation gates, complete-by-default capture, deterministic transcript reconstruction, a generic native JSON-to-LiNo serializer, and a read-only OpenCode SQLite adapter that feeds the same serializer. Diagnostic output remains verbose by default with an explicit global `--silent` opt-out.

The follow-up adds:

- `RecursiveTask`, `TaskExecutor`, and `solve_recursively`, with bounded depth/attempts and an explicit failure-driven back-edge;
- `learning_trace` on verified symbolic completions, recursive extraction from reported JSON/string envelopes, and review-gated proposal staging;
- exact approved-lesson recall in the solver, backed by the canonical promoted ledger and cached to keep routing latency bounded;
- regressions covering parent-to-leaf recovery, report ingestion, real symbolic-candidate round trip, and repeated-failure live recall;
- an executable Agent CLI replay and durable session evidence for the authored learning-ledger leaf.

The learning endpoint intentionally does **not** auto-promote uploaded material: reports can propose learnable rules, but promotion still requires human approval and benchmark evidence.

## Reproduction and verification

The original issue-822 regressions cover pre-confirmation creation, missing context selection, incomplete/indexed transcripts, opt-in logging, absent verbosity controls, generic conversion, OpenCode extraction, cumulative/incremental merging, final streamed responses, and stable ordering.

The recursive-learning regressions first demonstrated that the described loop was disconnected. They now prove that a failed parent shrinks to leaves and climbs back up, an uploaded complete trace reaches synthesis without bypassing review, a real symbolic candidate survives report serialization, and a repeated unknown uses the promoted lesson rather than deriving it again.

Validation performed on the final tree:

- `cargo test --all-features --test integration -- --test-threads=4` — 172 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --test unit issue_823_recursive_learning -- --nocapture` — 4 passed, 0 failed
- all-feature unit and doc-test targets passed in the complete suite run
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- self-AST regeneration and all 9 self-AST tests
- optimized release build
- real Formal AI server + Agent CLI replay with byte-for-byte ledger comparison

The first unconstrained integration run exposed three socket timeouts in issue-712 routing. The root cause was reconstructing and promoting the canonical ledger for every unknown attempt; caching that immutable approved ledger removed the repeated work, all six exact issue-712 regressions passed serially, and the final full integration target passed above.

## Release and self-hosting evidence

A `minor` changelog fragment covers the API/CLI/reporting capabilities. Version modification remains delegated to release automation. No visual UI changed, so screenshots are not applicable.

The new recursive decomposition names five smallest leaves. The real Agent CLI authored leaf L5, producing exactly the canonical promoted learning ledger, so the strict task metric is `1/5 = 20%`; manually authored leaves are not relabeled as self-coded. The paired commit trailers reference session `ses_075888666ffeU9fXsH9GrDSJ4k` and its committed [Agent stream evidence](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-822-b85211754f9e/docs/case-studies/issue-822/recursive-self-coding/agent-stream.jsonl).

The complete [issue #822 case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-822-b85211754f9e/docs/case-studies/issue-822) contains the reproductions, decomposition, prior full-context evidence, and recursive self-coding provenance.

After the recursive additions, the legacy changed-line release ratchet initially projected a drop from `17.14%` to `16.90%`. Four additional genuine Agent CLI leaves then produced 198 LiNo lines across source projection, rebuild/reattach guidance, self-explanation, and a reviewable change request. Their four real sessions and paired evidence trailers are preserved in the [ratchet recovery artifact bundle](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-822-b85211754f9e/docs/case-studies/issue-822/ratchet-self-coding), preserving both honest task attribution and the release ratchet without relabeling manually authored work.

Fixes #844.

## Outcome

This turns multi-source summarization into one inspectable links network rather than a shorter list of sentences:

- one `MergedStatement` per fact, with reversible receipts back to every absorbed source sentence;
- source-authority-aware ranking, probabilities, and explicit mutual `Contradicts` edges;
- bounded recursive gathering over exact, replayable `SourceCapture`s;
- a named `world_model::Context` audited by the shared, disproof-first `FactChecker` before presentation;
- deterministic full/standard/short/topic/identifier output;
- a deterministic learning proposal assembled from captures, merge receipts, contradictions, and the fact-check audit, with promotion still gated on human review.

The earlier fixture-only seam is no longer presented as production behavior. With #702, #843, and #845 now on `main`, `execute_multi_source_summary` composes `CachedSourceClient` → exact-capture classifier → recursive gather → named context → `FactChecker` → checked presentation → proposal-only learning. Capture failures remain diagnostics and never become evidence; a warm cache reproduces the checked summary and learning proposal offline without transport calls.

## Root cause and reproduction

The issue's acceptance cases were written before the implementation. They exposed these concrete faults:

1. `SourceCache` keyed bodies by digest but lost per-URL provenance, allowing an unoriginal mirror to inherit a first-party source tier.
2. Contradictory saturated evidence made `Context::recalculate` oscillate as `x ← 1 - x` until the pass limit, so both a claim and its denial could be reported as probable. Repeated states are now detected and collapsed to a verified fixpoint; equally authoritative opposites settle at `0.5`.
3. `formalize` treated every period as a sentence boundary, splitting tokens such as `crates.io` into a spurious extra fact.
4. Ranking counted raw source repetition but not source authority. Enough unoriginal mirrors could therefore outrank a single first-party statement even though mirrors correctly contributed zero truth probability. Ranking now combines coverage, average authority, and trust-weighted stance; unoriginal assertions contribute zero ranking evidence and unoriginal denials cannot demote trusted claims.

The minimal red logs and the complete worked output are preserved in `docs/case-studies/issue-844/`. `cargo run --example issue_844_statement_merge` exercises the Stack Overflow-style citation cycle, fixpoint stop, warm-cache replay, contradiction reporting, and every summarization rung. `cargo run --example issue_844_captured_pipeline` exercises the real exact-capture boundary, named fact-check audit, offline replay, and review-gated learning proposal.

## Main implementation

| Area | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `summarization::dedup` | Conservative statement signatures, retractable `MergeLink`s, disagreement edges, and `DedupReport::split`. |
| `summarization::importance` | Kind prior blended with observed coverage, integer source authority, and trust-weighted stance. |
| `summarization::gathering` | Shared unmet-difference traversal plus production exact-capture adapter; fixpoint and depth-bound termination. |
| `summarization::context` | Ranked facts translated into an explicitly named `Context` with provenance and contradiction links. |
| `summarization::pipeline` | Exact capture through checked presentation and deterministic proposal-only learning. |
| `summarization::recheck` | Compatibility preflight for already-materialized observations; production uses `FactChecker`. |
| `summarization::identifier` | New bottom rung with naming convention, reserved-word rejection, and a length budget. |

The merge remains deliberately conservative: wording-only differences merge, while stemming is not used. A missed merge loses concision; a wrong merge fabricates a fact.

Reader-facing evidence wording is seed data in English, Russian, Hindi, and Chinese. Trace records remain language-neutral `name=value` fields. The hardcoded-language allowlist was not expanded.

## Formal AI / Agent CLI evidence

- Same-task session `ses_050f9a572ffefpehWRjysug6cv` authored and verified the smallest implementation leaf through the external Agent CLI. The reviewed decomposition records one of five leaves as Agent-CLI-authored (20%); the implementation remains honestly human-authored otherwise.
- Final merged-tree self-AST session `ses_050768970ffexBZYa9Fh6slPbM` regenerated the live 349-document census through the real Agent CLI. It rewrote the three affected AST documents, and the exact committed census regeneration test passes.
- Closure audit: 2,412 defined meanings, 292 roles, 2,824 values, 0 unresolved references.
- Self-hosting evidence check: 33.07% (4,257 / 12,873 changed lines; 8 / 28 commits).

Raw client streams, server traces, session records, deterministic artifacts, and reproducible harnesses are under `docs/case-studies/issue-844/` and `experiments/`.

## Verification

- Red-first regressions: 27 issue-844 tests pass, including exact capture failure handling, live/offline replay, citation cycles, contradiction fixpoints, authority-aware ordering, unoriginal mirrors, split/retraction, language data, identifier budgets, and same-task Agent CLI evidence.
- Full all-features run with bounded host concurrency: **3,003 passed, 0 failed, 3 intentionally ignored** (main unit target: 2,229 passed).
- Clippy: all targets, all features, warnings denied.
- Formatting, locked metadata, docs/docs.rs, doctests, file-size and hardcoded-language guards, self-AST regeneration, total closure, secrets scan, and both examples pass.
- `origin/main` is an ancestor of the tested head; the working tree was clean before push.

This is not a UI change, so screenshots are not applicable.

## Documentation and release

- `docs/case-studies/issue-844/README.md` explains the production boundaries, failure modes, conservative merge rationale, worked examples, self-hosting evidence, and traceability.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-844/requirements.md` maps R844-01…R844-14 to named regression tests; a parser test fails if a mapped test is missing.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` records the global requirements.
- The changelog fragment requests a minor release.
title: Summarization: compose exact source captures into a checked context

Fixes #495

## Summary

- Add a seed-backed `behavior_rules_count` intent for supported-language count questions such as `Сколько всего правил?`, `How many behavior rules are there?`, `कुल कितने नियम हैं?`, and `总共有多少规则?`.
- Count built-in behavior rules plus dialog-local rules compiled from earlier user turns, and render the answer with explicit reasoning and `links` metadata for `built_in_rules`, `dialog_local_rules`, `total_rules`, and the counting algorithm.
- Mirror the count handling in the Rust solver, the browser worker, and the local browser fallback; regenerate the embedded web bundle.
- Resolve the latest `main` merge conflicts by integrating the count flow with the newer behavior-rule follow-up modules.
- Add multilingual regression coverage, including the reported Russian follow-up flow and a runtime-rule count case.

## Reproduction

Before this change, the reported prompt `Сколько всего правил?` routed to `unknown` even after listing behavior rules. A focused regression test initially failed with `intent = unknown` for the Russian count question.
